    # DryMDF macOS Desktop Migration

    **Status, 25 November 2026.** The single-file desktop editor and offline exports have recorded local verification. The Penpot redesign, multi-file workspaces, AI, and clean-Mac release checks are outstanding. The current build-output DMG path contains a Finder alias. Verify the actual image before using it for installation or distribution.

    ## Goal and release scope

    Ship DryMDF as an offline, single-user macOS app. Users should be able to install it from a DMG, open or write Markdown, preview it, and export PDF, HTML, and Markdown with no hosted backend.

    The first release targets **Apple Silicon** and uses a **free, unnotarized DMG** hosted on GitHub Releases. The download instructions will cover the first-launch **Open Anyway** prompt. Windows, Intel Macs, notarization, App Store distribution, automatic updates, and cloud sync are deferred. Record the oldest macOS version that passes installer and export testing before publishing.

    ## Architecture and code changes

    - **Desktop shell.** Add an Electron and Electron Forge workspace at `apps/desktop`. Package a static build of the editor from `apps/frontend` and launch into the editor. Reuse CodeMirror, the split-pane preview, theming, and Zustand. Check that routing, CSS, fonts, and other assets load from the installed bundle. Keep the current web build usable during migration.
    - **Local conversion.** Add a typed desktop bridge for conversion and file dialogs. Wire both the export handler in [the editor](../apps/frontend/src/app/editor/page.tsx) and the generated PDF path in [the preview pane](../apps/frontend/src/components/preview/pdf-preview-pane.tsx) to it. Desktop runtime dependencies should consist of the packaged app and its local assets. Drop the HTTP calls, Bull/Redis jobs, and WebSocket status polling from the desktop paths.
    - **PDF layout.** Reuse the existing [print styles and footer](../apps/backend/src/modules/pdf/print-layout.ts). Generate preview and export with the same hidden Chromium window and `webContents.printToPDF` pipeline. Bundle Mermaid, KaTeX CSS and fonts, syntax highlighting, and print fonts locally. Wait for diagrams, fonts, and supported images before printing. Discard stale preview results when the document or options change, and release temporary resources after each job.
    - **File access and safety.** Add native Open and Save dialogs and preserve draft recovery across restarts. Keep file reads and writes in the main process and validate requests from the renderer. Treat imported Markdown and Mermaid as untrusted content. Use sandboxed renderers, context isolation, a narrow preload bridge, sanitized HTML, and restricted navigation. Support relative images from the opened document's folder. Define a clear placeholder for unavailable remote images and verify that preview and export work offline.

    The first usable redesign is Phase 1. Phase 2 makes it a multi-file editor, and Phase 5 completes the AI workflow. Keep cross-file writes, indexing, automatic tool execution, and additional hosted adapters outside this release.

    ## Multi-file workspaces and editor AI

    - **Workspaces:** Create a named workspace, then add Markdown files through the native picker. Show them in a sidebar with the active file and unsaved changes. Keep originals in place, save each file independently, and restore drafts after quitting. Handle missing or externally changed files before overwriting.
    - **AI settings:** Offer Ollama and LM Studio as local presets and one hosted OpenAI-compatible provider with an API key. Show where inference runs, list models, and offer a connection test with a fixed test prompt. Keep keys in Keychain-backed storage through Electron's main process, scoped to the provider and endpoint. Verify access across updates to the ad-hoc-signed DMG.
    - **Local routing:** Connect to loopback for local presets. Surface server unavailable, no models, and authentication errors. Treat Ollama cloud models as remote and require a hosted choice for them. Keep hosted requests on HTTPS and keep document data and keys out of logs.
    - **In-editor AI:** Default to the text selection when one exists. Offer explicit controls for the active file or named workspace files. Show the provider, model, and selected context before sending, with a clear disclosure for hosted requests. Stream responses with a Stop action. Present document edits as diffs with Apply and Discard and put applied edits on the editor's undo stack. If the source changed while AI was running, regenerate the suggestion against the new text.
    - **Launch scope:** Local AI downloads and runs through the user's chosen provider app. Editing and export work with AI disabled. Cross-file writes, workspace indexing, tool execution, and additional hosted adapters are deferred.

    Dossier provides a reference for provider selection, model discovery, endpoint-scoped keys, and connection testing. DryMDF's desktop bridge owns provider calls and only receives document context selected by the user.

    ## Build and install the test DMG

    Use Apple Silicon macOS, Node 22.12 or newer within the 22.x line, and the repository's pinned pnpm version. From the repository root, run:

    ```sh
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make
    ```

    Open `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg`, drag DryMDF into Applications, and launch it. If macOS blocks the first launch because it cannot verify the developer, try opening DryMDF first, then use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. [Apple's installation instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445)

    The build applies a local ad-hoc signature, verifies the app bundle, runs the packaged executable in headless mode, and writes a `.sha256` file next to the DMG. The direct download remains unnotarized.

    ## First-launch setup

    - The welcome flow introduces the editor, offline exports, and file access. It can be skipped or reopened with **Setup** in the desktop toolbar.
    - DryMDF receives file access through the macOS Open and Save dialogs. Relative images are read within the selected document's folder.
    - Export notifications start off. Users can opt in, send a test notification, and change their preference from **Setup**. macOS controls banner delivery under **System Settings → Notifications**. The editor reports export results in the app.
    - [x] Verify first launch, skip, relaunch, reopening Setup, and persisting the notification choice.
    - [x] Verify a test request and successful export route through the desktop bridge after opt-in. Verify opt-out stops export requests.
    - [ ] On a clean Mac, test notification delivery after allowing it and verify exports work after denying it.

    ## Milestone acceptance

    ### Internal beta

    - [x] A packaged Apple Silicon build opens directly into the editor.
    - [x] An offline multi-page Markdown fixture renders and exports with Mermaid, KaTeX, and a JavaScript code block. A separate PDF probe verifies page numbers.
    - [x] PDF preview and saved PDF agree on page count and pagination for the fixture.

    ### Release MVP

    - [x] Users can create and edit Markdown, open a local `.md` file, and save PDF, HTML, and Markdown to a chosen folder offline. Local images, Unicode filenames, and paths with spaces work.
    - [x] Page size, background, and available page numbering options behave consistently in preview and export. Multi-page content has no clipped diagrams or text.
    - [x] Draft content returns after relaunch. Canceling a dialog leaves the document and destination untouched. A failed export surfaces an actionable error and permits a retry.
    - [ ] Create and reopen a workspace with multiple Markdown files, retain each draft separately, and handle a moved file and an external edit safely.
    - [ ] Test model discovery, successful chat, and recovery from a stopped local server with both Ollama and LM Studio. Test one hosted provider with a user-supplied key and verify keys stay scoped to the configured endpoint across restart and update.
    - [ ] Verify selection-only and explicitly added file context, hosted disclosure, stream cancellation, diff Apply and Discard, undo, and stale suggestion handling.
    - [ ] Download the release-candidate DMG through a browser on a clean Apple Silicon Mac. Drag DryMDF into Applications, verify the first-launch override with Gatekeeper enabled, then rerun offline export from the installed copy.
    - [ ] Publish the exact tested DMG with its SHA-256 checksum, supported macOS version, and install steps. If macOS blocks first launch because it cannot verify the developer, direct users to **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** after they try to open DryMDF. [Apple's installation instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445)

    - **Setup:** Hidden-window tests verified onboarding, persistence, notification opt-in and opt-out, and export notification requests using a simulated notification service. Native banner delivery and the first-run system prompt still require visible testing.

    For each release candidate, record the build tag, DMG checksum, tested macOS version and hardware, fixture used, results, and linked follow-up issues.

    # Coding rules

    ## A PR does only its ticket's job (read before working in any repo)
    - Before writing code, state the ticket's problem in one line and the exact failing case(s). The PR fixes those cases and nothing else.
    - Make the smallest diff that fixes them. No widening to sibling phrasings or features, no refactors, no "while I'm here" changes.
    - Everything outside the ticket keeps the base branch's behaviour exactly. Run probes and sibling checks to prove nothing outside the scope changed, not to find more to fix.
    - Inside the ticket, the fix must work the way users actually phrase the failing case: natural variants, the question's own words echoed back, short forms. Test those too. That is the ticket's case, not widening.
    - When a review finds a gap outside the ticket's case, narrow: fall back to the base branch's behaviour. Don't extend the fix. Wider coverage goes in a follow-up issue, linked in the PR body.
    - Never narrow the ticket's own case to its literal phrasing, or retitle the PR to dodge a general rule. The ticket's case must work in its common form.
    - Test on the merge result with the current base branch, not only on the branch. Never push after approval without a new approval. No PR may depend on another unmerged PR.
    - The PR title and body describe the ticket's fix only. Don't grow them past it.
    - Review replies answer each finding and say what changed and how it is tested. They add no new scope and no extra work.
    - When briefing a subagent on a PR, put the ticket's exact case and this scope rule in the brief. List what must work as well as what must not change.

    ## Verify before every push (any repo)
    - **Mutation testing covers every alternative.** In a new or rewritten regex, word set or enum, drop each word, each character class and each branch on its own. Don't stop at the ones a reviewer named.
    - **"Changed" includes changed jobs.** If the push removes or skips a check, mutate and test the older line that is now the only guard for that case, even though its text didn't change.
    - **Time limits cut test scope, not mutants.** Keep sweeps short by running only the PR's own test files, never by skipping mutants.
    - **Fix the category, not the row.** When a probe or mutant finds a bad case, name the class it belongs to and fix that, with two or more tests from the class. Narrowing one word to dodge the found row is a one-case fix.

    ## Reuse before adding
    - Don't repeat code. Before writing a helper, branch or constant, search for an existing one and call it.
    - Change existing code at its call site rather than copying it into a new function.
    - Add a new block only when nothing existing can do the job. Keep it small, and have the old code use it too so there is one copy, not two.

    ## Use existing checkouts
    - Before cloning or downloading repository source, check for an existing local checkout, including in `~/Desktop/projects/open-source-contributes`. Use the checkout the user provides. Ask before downloading another copy.

    # Shared memory (all AI tools)
    The vault is ~/Brain. It is the single memory store for every AI tool. Do not keep a separate copy anywhere else.
    - Isolation: ~/Brain/_index/routing.md maps the working directory to exactly one project. Read only that project's hub and notes. Never read other projects' notes, Home.md, or search the whole vault, unless the user asks. If the directory is not in routing.md, ask which project to use. Never copy facts from one project into another.
    - Save durable facts to projects/<project>/facts/<slug>.md (only in the routed project) and decisions to projects/<project>/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md. One fact or decision per file.
    - Frontmatter on every note: name, description, project, type (user|feedback|project|reference|decision), source (claude|codex|gemini|other), date.
    - Link every note to its project hub and to related notes with wikilinks (double square brackets). A hub must link every note in its project. Update an existing note rather than adding a duplicate.
    - Skills live in ~/.agents/skills. MCP servers are defined in ~/Brain/_config/mcp/servers.json. Hook scripts live in ~/Brain/_config/hooks.
    - Never store secrets or tokens in the vault.

    ### Release MVP

    - [x] Users can create and edit Markdown, open a local `.md` file, and save PDF, HTML, and Markdown to a chosen folder offline. Local images, Unicode filenames, and paths with spaces work.
    - [x] Page size, background, and available page numbering options behave consistently in preview and export. Multi-page content has no clipped diagrams or text.
    - [x] Draft content returns after relaunch. Canceling a dialog leaves the document and destination untouched. A failed export surfaces an actionable error and permits a retry.
    - [ ] Create and reopen a workspace with multiple Markdown files, retain each draft separately, and handle a moved file and an external edit safely.
    - [ ] Test model discovery, successful chat, and recovery from a stopped local server with both Ollama and LM Studio. Test one hosted provider with a user-supplied key and verify keys stay scoped to the configured endpoint across restart and update.
    - [ ] Verify selection-only and explicitly added file context, hosted disclosure, stream cancellation, diff Apply and Discard, undo, and stale suggestion handling.
    - [ ] Download the release-candidate DMG through a browser on a clean Apple Silicon Mac. Drag DryMDF into Applications, verify the first-launch override with Gatekeeper enabled, then rerun offline export from the installed copy.
    - [ ] Publish the exact tested DMG with its SHA-256 checksum, supported macOS version, and install steps. If macOS blocks first launch because it cannot verify the developer, direct users to **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** after they try to open DryMDF. [Apple's installation instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445)

    ## Verification log

    ### Local test build 0.1.0

    - **Environment:** Apple Silicon, macOS 27.0.1. The DMG passed integrity verification and mounted successfully. The app was copied from the DMG into a temporary install directory.
    - **Offline result:** With network requests disabled in the editor, PDF preview and export each produced six A4 pages with matching extracted page text. Both PDFs included the Mermaid diagram, embedded KaTeX fonts, and the code block. A separate PDF contained page numbers 1 through 6. The normal web build also passed.

    ### Release candidate 0.1.0

    - **Installer:** `DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg` passed integrity verification and launched after being copied from the mounted image. Verified on Apple Silicon running macOS 27.0.1. SHA-256 is `112031af19a69c917c1ca69e02443080f2497ed02678ab0058fc5fb66fbf80d4`.
    - **Files:** Opened Markdown with Unicode in the filename and spaces in the path. A relative PNG rendered offline and returned with the draft after relaunch. Verified the macOS Save sheet on the installed app. Export tests used controlled Save selections to verify cancellation, failure, and retry.
    - **Exports:** PDF preview and saved PDF matched across four A4 pages, with all 32 sections, a relative image, a Mermaid diagram, and embedded KaTeX fonts. A separate Legal fixture verified the page color and footer numbering. HTML reopened offline with its embedded image, diagrams, math fonts, and highlighting. Markdown round-tripped exactly.
    - **Web:** The frontend and backend builds passed. Compared the extracted print styles and footer with the original web implementation for default and customized options.
    - **Pending:** Browser download and first launch with Gatekeeper on a clean Apple Silicon Mac, testing the oldest macOS version claimed for release, and publishing the DMG and checksum.

    ### Release candidate with first-launch setup

    - **Installer:** SHA-256 is `8cadd1d7b4c601221dfb2bc724b813dcab58acc608b9c9beda857c67cc936374`. The previous ad-hoc signature enabled Hardened Runtime, causing macOS to reject the bundled Electron framework at startup. The rebuilt DMG uses per-file ad-hoc signing settings and checks the actual executable before creating the image.
    - **Setup:** Hidden-window tests verified onboarding, persistence, notification opt-in and opt-out, and export notification requests using a simulated notification service. Native banner delivery and the first-run system prompt still require visible testing.

    For each release candidate, record the build tag, DMG checksum, tested macOS version and hardware, fixture used, results, and linked follow-up issues.
    ## Future Enhancements (Post-Launch)

    1. **User Accounts** - Save documents to cloud
    2. **Collaboration** - Real-time multi-user editing (Yjs/CRDT)
    3. **Templates Library** - Pre-built document templates
    4. **Version History** - Document revision tracking
    5. **Image Upload** - Direct image embedding with S3
    6. **Public API** - API keys for integrations
    7. **Custom Mermaid Themes** - User-defined diagram styles
    8. **CLI Tool** - Command-line PDF generation
    9. **VS Code Extension** - Export from VS Code
    10. **Self-hosting** - Docker images for self-hosting

    ## First-launch setup

    - The welcome flow introduces the editor, offline exports, and file access. It can be skipped or reopened with **Setup** in the desktop toolbar.
    - DryMDF receives file access through the macOS Open and Save dialogs. Relative images are read within the selected document's folder.
    - Export notifications start off. Users can opt in, send a test notification, and change their preference from **Setup**. macOS controls banner delivery under **System Settings → Notifications**. The editor reports export results in the app.
    - [x] Verify first launch, skip, relaunch, reopening Setup, and persisting the notification choice.
    - [x] Verify a test request and successful export route through the desktop bridge after opt-in. Verify opt-out stops export requests.
    - [ ] On a clean Mac, test notification delivery after allowing it and verify exports work after denying it.

    - [x] A packaged Apple Silicon build opens directly into the editor.

    # Coding rules

    ## A PR does only its ticket's job (read before working in any repo)
    - Before writing code, state the ticket's problem in one line and the exact failing case(s). The PR fixes those cases and nothing else.
    - Make the smallest diff that fixes them. No widening to sibling phrasings or features, no refactors, no "while I'm here" changes.
    - Everything outside the ticket keeps the base branch's behaviour exactly. Run probes and sibling checks to prove nothing outside the scope changed, not to find more to fix.
    - Inside the ticket, the fix must work the way users actually phrase the failing case: natural variants, the question's own words echoed back, short forms. Test those too. That is the ticket's case, not widening.
    - When a review finds a gap outside the ticket's case, narrow: fall back to the base branch's behaviour. Don't extend the fix. Wider coverage goes in a follow-up issue, linked in the PR body.
    - Never narrow the ticket's own case to its literal phrasing, or retitle the PR to dodge a general rule. The ticket's case must work in its common form.
    - Test on the merge result with the current base branch, not only on the branch. Never push after approval without a new approval. No PR may depend on another unmerged PR.
    - The PR title and body describe the ticket's fix only. Don't grow them past it.
    - Review replies answer each finding and say what changed and how it is tested. They add no new scope and no extra work.
    - When briefing a subagent on a PR, put the ticket's exact case and this scope rule in the brief. List what must work as well as what must not change.

    ## Verify before every push (any repo)
    - **Mutation testing covers every alternative.** In a new or rewritten regex, word set or enum, drop each word, each character class and each branch on its own. Don't stop at the ones a reviewer named.
    - **"Changed" includes changed jobs.** If the push removes or skips a check, mutate and test the older line that is now the only guard for that case, even though its text didn't change.
    - **Time limits cut test scope, not mutants.** Keep sweeps short by running only the PR's own test files, never by skipping mutants.
    - **Fix the category, not the row.** When a probe or mutant finds a bad case, name the class it belongs to and fix that, with two or more tests from the class. Narrowing one word to dodge the found row is a one-case fix.

    ## Reuse before adding
    - Don't repeat code. Before writing a helper, branch or constant, search for an existing one and call it.
    - Change existing code at its call site rather than copying it into a new function.
    - Add a new block only when nothing existing can do the job. Keep it small, and have the old code use it too so there is one copy, not two.

    ## Use existing checkouts
    - Before cloning or downloading repository source, check for an existing local checkout, including in `~/Desktop/projects/open-source-contributes`. Use the checkout the user provides. Ask before downloading another copy.

    # Shared memory (all AI tools)
    There are two vaults. They are never mixed, and each is the single memory store for its own work. Do not keep a separate copy anywhere else.
    - **Personal vault: ~/Brain.** Personal and side projects only. Never write anything about JUTEQ work in it: no JUTEQ code, tickets, PRs, reviews, reviewers, decisions, customers, repos or notes, even when asked to "save this decision" while working in a JUTEQ directory. Do not add JUTEQ directories to its routing.md.
    - **JUTEQ vault: /Users/ajaymandal/Desktop/juteq/WorkVault.** Everything about JUTEQ work, all projects (argus, autorail, autorail-agents-v2, autorail-fe, autorail-mua and any new one). Same layout and rules as the personal vault, with its own _index/routing.md and _index/PROTOCOL.md.
    - Pick the vault from the working directory: anything under ~/Desktop/juteq is the JUTEQ vault, everything else is the personal vault. If it is unclear, ask. Never copy facts from one vault into the other.
    Rules for the routed vault (read its _index/PROTOCOL.md for the full text):
    - Isolation: the vault's _index/routing.md maps the working directory to exactly one project. Read only that project's hub and notes. Never read other projects' notes, Home.md, or search the whole vault, unless the user asks. If the directory is not in routing.md, ask which project to use.
    - Save durable facts to projects/<project>/facts/<slug>.md (only in the routed project) and decisions to projects/<project>/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md. One fact or decision per file.
    - Frontmatter on every note: name, description, project, type (user|feedback|project|reference|decision), source (claude|codex|gemini|other), date.
    - Link every note to its project hub and to related notes with wikilinks (double square brackets). A hub must link every note in its project. Update an existing note rather than adding a duplicate.
    - Skills live in ~/.agents/skills. MCP servers are defined in ~/Brain/_config/mcp/servers.json and hook scripts live in ~/Brain/_config/hooks; the JUTEQ vault has no tool config of its own.
    - Never store secrets or tokens in a vault.

    ## Recorded verification

    - An installed Apple Silicon build on macOS 27.0.1 produced matching six-page A4 preview and PDF export with the network disabled. Mermaid, KaTeX fonts, code, and page numbering were checked.
    - The 0.1.0 release candidate DMG mounted and launched. Unicode paths, spaces, a relative PNG, draft recovery, native Save, cancel, failure, and retry were checked. A separate four-page fixture matched preview and export, and a Legal PDF verified background color and number placement. HTML opened offline and Markdown round-tripped exactly.
    - Frontend and backend builds passed in the recorded release candidate run. Web print styles and footer output were checked against the earlier implementation for default and customized options.
    - First-launch setup passed hidden-window tests for skip, reopen, saved preferences, and simulated notification opt-in and opt-out. Native permission prompts and banner delivery still need a visible clean-Mac test.
    - An earlier signing build failed to launch because Hardened Runtime caused macOS to reject the bundled Electron framework. The recorded rebuild adopted per-file ad-hoc signing and checks the executable before creating the image.

    On 2026-11-25, the file at `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg` was 134,749,237 bytes. Its SHA-256 matched the sidecar:

    ```text
    8c9010e33e99aa3aa4355b469803fecd3644e9c2e4d7f7f322686e92354080e5
    ```

    The migration plan’s alias warning describes an earlier file at this path. Earlier mount and launch evidence refers to different checksums. The current bytes still need an installation and export run tied to their checksum and source revision.

    # DryMDF desktop release scope

    The first desktop release targets a single-user, offline editor on Apple Silicon macOS. Publish a free, unnotarized DMG through GitHub Releases with its SHA-256, supported macOS version, and first-launch instructions. Determine the oldest supported macOS through installer and export testing. Editing and PDF, HTML, and Markdown export work with AI disabled.

    The redesigned MVP includes multi-file workspaces, the Penpot editor and export flows, and opt-in AI through Ollama, LM Studio, or one hosted OpenAI-compatible provider. Defer Windows, Intel Macs, notarization, App Store distribution, automatic updates, cloud sync, cross-file AI writes, workspace indexing, AI tool execution, and additional hosted adapters.

    # DryMDF macOS Desktop Migration

    **Status, 25 November 2026.** The single-file desktop editor and offline exports have recorded local verification. The Penpot redesign, multi-file workspaces, AI, and clean-Mac release checks are outstanding. The current build-output DMG path contains a Finder alias. Verify the actual image before using it for installation or distribution.

    ## Goal and release scope

    Ship DryMDF as an offline, single-user macOS app. Users should be able to install it from a DMG, open or write Markdown, preview it, and export PDF, HTML, and Markdown with no hosted backend.

    The first release targets **Apple Silicon** and uses a **free, unnotarized DMG** hosted on GitHub Releases. The download instructions will cover the first-launch **Open Anyway** prompt. Windows, Intel Macs, notarization, App Store distribution, automatic updates, and cloud sync are deferred. Record the oldest macOS version that passes installer and export testing before publishing.

    ## Architecture and code changes

    - **Desktop shell.** Add an Electron and Electron Forge workspace at `apps/desktop`. Package a static build of the editor from `apps/frontend` and launch into the editor. Reuse CodeMirror, the split-pane preview, theming, and Zustand. Check that routing, CSS, fonts, and other assets load from the installed bundle. Keep the current web build usable during migration.
    - **Local conversion.** Add a typed desktop bridge for conversion and file dialogs. Wire both the export handler in [the editor](../apps/frontend/src/app/editor/page.tsx) and the generated PDF path in [the preview pane](../apps/frontend/src/components/preview/pdf-preview-pane.tsx) to it. Desktop runtime dependencies should consist of the packaged app and its local assets. Drop the HTTP calls, Bull/Redis jobs, and WebSocket status polling from the desktop paths.
    - **PDF layout.** Reuse the existing [print styles and footer](../apps/backend/src/modules/pdf/print-layout.ts). Generate preview and export with the same hidden Chromium window and `webContents.printToPDF` pipeline. Bundle Mermaid, KaTeX CSS and fonts, syntax highlighting, and print fonts locally. Wait for diagrams, fonts, and supported images before printing. Discard stale preview results when the document or options change, and release temporary resources after each job.
    - **File access and safety.** Add native Open and Save dialogs and preserve draft recovery across restarts. Keep file reads and writes in the main process and validate requests from the renderer. Treat imported Markdown and Mermaid as untrusted content. Use sandboxed renderers, context isolation, a narrow preload bridge, sanitized HTML, and restricted navigation. Support relative images from the opened document's folder. Define a clear placeholder for unavailable remote images and verify that preview and export work offline.

    ## Phased delivery from the Penpot design

    Reviewed the local working tree and the open Penpot file _New File 1_ on 25 November 2026. Its 32 boards span Direction, Identity, First launch, Workspace, Export and settings, Multi-file workspaces, and AI in the editor. MAC-01–04 describe the existing single-file implementation. Their verification log records earlier runs. The checks below define when the redesigned app is ready.

    ### Phase 0 — Establish a reproducible baseline

    - Start with the current working tree. The desktop workspace and some shared print and frontend changes are still untracked or uncommitted. Capture the intended baseline before branching feature tickets.
    - At inspection, `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg` was a 668-byte macOS alias whose SHA-256 differed from its sidecar. Locate the original image or build a fresh one. Verify its checksum and mount it before installing.
    - **Pass when** the installed copy opens the existing draft, previews and exports the offline fixture, and the web editor still builds. Record the revision and actual image checksum so later phases can repeat the comparison.

    ### Phase 1 — Deliver the desktop editor shell and first launch (MAC-09)

    - Use the Two Sheets icon from Identity for the app bundle and installer, with the separate wordmark on Welcome. Check the silhouette at 16, 32, and 128 pt in light and dark appearances. The Page Fold board is the design fallback if small-size legibility fails.
    - Use the Direction board’s system type, Monaco source text, blue selection, and thin dividers. At the 1080 × 690 reference size, place navigation on the left, Markdown in the center, and preview on the right. At 720 × 660, switch between Editor and Preview. The current [split pane](../apps/frontend/src/components/layout/split-pane.tsx) stacks both at narrow widths. Reuse CodeMirror and the existing preview components.
    - Implement Start, Recents, New Document, Open a File, and the editable sample with Start Over / Start Editing. Preserve Skip Setup and the existing draft on upgrade. Populate Recents from real opens. Workspace navigation becomes available with Phase 2.
    - **Pass when** first launch, skip, canceled Open, sample editing, and relaunch all lead to the intended document. Compare the packaged app with the light, dark, and compact boards. Verify keyboard access, focus return, and reduced motion and transparency.

    ### Phase 2 — Make workspaces reliable (MAC-06)

    - Implement Library → Create Workspace → Add Files → editor sidebar. Keep originals in place. Persist workspace membership, recent use, active file, and a stable ID per document. Migrate the existing single draft together with its local-image association. The [editor store](../apps/frontend/src/stores/editor-store.ts) currently persists one document and the [file bridge](../apps/desktop/documents.cjs) records one image root.
    - Track saved revisions and recoverable drafts separately. Make Save write the selected document. Keep its dirty indicator until that write succeeds. For external changes or a missing file, offer Keep Draft, Reload from Disk, or Locate File as applicable.
    - **Pass when** two files with the same name in different folders retain independent drafts and relative images after switching and quitting. Saving one changes only its original. Move one file and externally edit the other, then exercise each recovery action and verify the resulting disk contents.

    ### Phase 3 — Complete page setup, export, and settings (MAC-10)

    - Connect the designed paper size, orientation, and margin controls to both preview and print. Orientation is missing from the current [PDF options](../apps/frontend/src/types/pdf.ts). Retain existing color and numbering options. Show Generate Preview when empty and Refresh PDF when edits make the preview stale.
    - Deliver the format, filename, destination, progress, completion, and retry sheets. Reuse the native save dialog. The current [preload bridge](../apps/desktop/preload.cjs) returns a success flag. Give Show in Finder a reference to the completed export and retain the user’s choices for Export Again or Choose Folder.
    - Move the notification offer from onboarding to after the first successful PDF export. Put appearance, restore last session, notification preference, system settings access, and test alert in Settings. Honor earlier opt-in and opt-out choices.
    - **Pass when** changing orientation or margins produces matching preview and saved PDF pagination, HTML opens offline, and Markdown round-trips. Canceling leaves the destination untouched. A failed save supports retry to another folder. Show in Finder reveals the file actually written.

    ### Phase 4 — Connect and verify AI providers (MAC-07)

    - This work can begin after Phase 0 alongside the desktop UI. Build the settings screens for Ollama, LM Studio, and one hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Support model discovery, model selection, refresh, and a fixed-prompt connection test using no document content. Show where inference runs and distinguish unavailable server, empty model list, and authentication failure.
    - Route provider calls through typed Electron main-process operations. Keep local presets on loopback with downloaded local models, route cloud models through an explicit hosted choice, and require HTTPS for hosted requests. Keep keys in Keychain-backed storage scoped to provider and endpoint. Keep prompts, document contents, and secrets out of logs.
    - **Pass when** each local provider lists models, streams a response, and recovers after a server restart. Test one hosted endpoint with a supplied key. Check a packaged upgrade retains access to that endpoint’s key and switching endpoints cannot reuse it. Editing and export must work with AI off.

    ### Phase 5 — Ship context-aware chat and reviewed edits (MAC-08)

    - After Phases 2 and 4, use the editor’s right pane for chat. Start with the selection. Let the user explicitly add the active document or named workspace files. Show the prompt, provider, model, and included context. For hosted requests, show the Penpot **Review before sending** sheet with Cancel and Send Context before transmitting document text.
    - Stream the reply with Stop and Retry. Bind a suggestion to its source document, revision, and selected range. Show Original and Suggestion with Apply Edit and Discard. Apply one undoable CodeMirror change to the source draft. If the user switches files or changes the source, prevent applying to the wrong text and offer regeneration for a stale suggestion.
    - **Pass when** a request with a paragraph from Ridge walk.md and an explicitly added Gear list.md excludes Weather.md and the rest of Ridge walk.md. Canceling hosted review sends nothing. Stopping ignores late tokens. Discard leaves the draft intact, Apply updates the preview, and Undo restores the exact original. Check typing and switching files mid-stream.

    ### Phase 6 — Qualify and publish the redesigned app (MAC-05)

    - Build from the integrated revision after Phases 1–5. Compare the installed surfaces with the Penpot reference boards, including compact navigation and error recovery. Repeat the existing offline export fixture, upgrade a single-file draft, and run the workspace and provider acceptance cases from the packaged app.
    - **Pass when** a browser-downloaded DMG installs on a clean Apple Silicon Mac with Gatekeeper enabled, notification allow and deny paths have been observed, and the oldest claimed macOS version has passed. Publish those exact tested bytes, SHA-256, supported OS, and installation steps.

    The first usable redesign is Phase 1. Phase 2 makes it a multi-file editor, and Phase 5 completes the AI workflow. Keep cross-file writes, indexing, automatic tool execution, and additional hosted adapters outside this release.

    ## Multi-file workspaces and editor AI

    - **Workspaces:** Create a named workspace, then add Markdown files through the native picker. Show them in a sidebar with the active file and unsaved changes. Keep originals in place, save each file independently, and restore drafts after quitting. Handle missing or externally changed files before overwriting.
    - **AI settings:** Offer Ollama and LM Studio as local presets and one hosted OpenAI-compatible provider with an API key. Show where inference runs, list models, and offer a connection test with a fixed test prompt. Keep keys in Keychain-backed storage through Electron's main process, scoped to the provider and endpoint. Verify access across updates to the ad-hoc-signed DMG.
    - **Local routing:** Connect to loopback for local presets. Surface server unavailable, no models, and authentication errors. Treat Ollama cloud models as remote and require a hosted choice for them. Keep hosted requests on HTTPS and keep document data and keys out of logs.
    - **In-editor AI:** Default to the text selection when one exists. Offer explicit controls for the active file or named workspace files. Show the provider, model, and selected context before sending, with a clear disclosure for hosted requests. Stream responses with a Stop action. Present document edits as diffs with Apply and Discard and put applied edits on the editor's undo stack. If the source changed while AI was running, regenerate the suggestion against the new text.
    - **Launch scope:** Local AI downloads and runs through the user's chosen provider app. Editing and export work with AI disabled. Cross-file writes, workspace indexing, tool execution, and additional hosted adapters are deferred.

    Dossier provides a reference for provider selection, model discovery, endpoint-scoped keys, and connection testing. DryMDF's desktop bridge owns provider calls and only receives document context selected by the user.

    ## Build and install the test DMG

    Use Apple Silicon macOS, Node 22.12 or newer within the 22.x line, and the repository's pinned pnpm version. From the repository root, run:

    ```sh
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make
    ```

    Open `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg`, drag DryMDF into Applications, and launch it. If macOS blocks the first launch because it cannot verify the developer, try opening DryMDF first, then use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. [Apple's installation instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445)

    The build applies a local ad-hoc signature, verifies the app bundle, runs the packaged executable in headless mode, and writes a `.sha256` file next to the DMG. The direct download remains unnotarized.

    ## First-launch setup

    - The welcome flow introduces the editor, offline exports, and file access. It can be skipped or reopened with **Setup** in the desktop toolbar.
    - DryMDF receives file access through the macOS Open and Save dialogs. Relative images are read within the selected document's folder.
    - Export notifications start off. Users can opt in, send a test notification, and change their preference from **Setup**. macOS controls banner delivery under **System Settings → Notifications**. The editor reports export results in the app.
    - [x] Verify first launch, skip, relaunch, reopening Setup, and persisting the notification choice.
    - [x] Verify a test request and successful export route through the desktop bridge after opt-in. Verify opt-out stops export requests.
    - [ ] On a clean Mac, test notification delivery after allowing it and verify exports work after denying it.

    - [x] PDF preview and saved PDF agree on page count and pagination for the fixture.

    ### Release MVP

    - [x] Users can create and edit Markdown, open a local `.md` file, and save PDF, HTML, and Markdown to a chosen folder offline. Local images, Unicode filenames, and paths with spaces work.
    - [x] Page size, background, and available page numbering options behave consistently in preview and export. Multi-page content has no clipped diagrams or text.
    - [x] Draft content returns after relaunch. Canceling a dialog leaves the document and destination untouched. A failed export surfaces an actionable error and permits a retry.
    - [ ] Create and reopen a workspace with multiple Markdown files, retain each draft separately, and handle a moved file and an external edit safely.
    - [ ] Test model discovery, successful chat, and recovery from a stopped local server with both Ollama and LM Studio. Test one hosted provider with a user-supplied key and verify keys stay scoped to the configured endpoint across restart and update.
    - [ ] Verify selection-only and explicitly added file context, hosted disclosure, stream cancellation, diff Apply and Discard, undo, and stale suggestion handling.
    - [ ] Download the release-candidate DMG through a browser on a clean Apple Silicon Mac. Drag DryMDF into Applications, verify the first-launch override with Gatekeeper enabled, then rerun offline export from the installed copy.
    - [ ] Publish the exact tested DMG with its SHA-256 checksum, supported macOS version, and install steps. If macOS blocks first launch because it cannot verify the developer, direct users to **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** after they try to open DryMDF. The rebuilt DMG uses per-file ad-hoc signing settings and checks the actual executable before creating the image.

    # DryMDF Web Application - Project Plan

    ## Executive Summary

    This document outlines the comprehensive development plan for building a production-ready, open-source Markdown to PDF converter web application. The application will enable users to write, edit, preview, and export Markdown documents to PDF and HTML formats.

    ## Real-time Job Processing Flow

    ```mermaid
    sequenceDiagram
        participant Client as Next.js Client
        participant WS as WebSocket
        participant API as NestJS API
        participant Queue as Bull Queue
        participant Worker as Job Processor

        participant Storage as S3/R2

        Client->>API: POST /convert/pdf
        API->>API: Validate DTO
        API->>API: Check Rate Limit
        API->>Queue: Add Job
        Queue-->>API: Job ID
        API-->>Client: { jobId, status: 'queued' }

        Client->>WS: Subscribe to job updates

        Queue->>Worker: Process Job
        Worker->>Worker: Parse Markdown (20%)
        Worker->>WS: Progress Update
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'parsing', progress: 20 }

        Worker->>Puppeteer: Render HTML + Mermaid
        Worker->>WS: Progress Update
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'rendering', progress: 50 }

        Puppeteer->>Puppeteer: Generate PDF
        Worker->>WS: Progress Update
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'generating', progress: 80 }

        Worker->>Storage: Upload PDF
        Storage-->>Worker: File URL
        Worker->>WS: Complete
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'complete', url: '...' }

        Client->>Storage: Download PDF
    ```

    ## State Management Flow

    ```mermaid
    stateDiagram-v2
        [*] --> Idle

        Idle --> Editing: User starts typing
        Editing --> Parsing: Content changed (debounced)
        Parsing --> PreviewReady: Parse complete
        Parsing --> RenderingMermaid: Mermaid blocks detected
        RenderingMermaid --> PreviewReady: Diagrams rendered
        PreviewReady --> Editing: User continues typing

        Editing --> Uploading: File dropped
        Uploading --> Editing: File content loaded
        Uploading --> Error: Upload failed

        PreviewReady --> Exporting: Export triggered
        Exporting --> Queued: Job submitted to backend
        Queued --> Processing: Job started
        Processing --> Generating: PDF/HTML generation
        Generating --> Downloading: Generation complete
        Downloading --> PreviewReady: Download started

        Queued --> Error: Queue failed
        Processing --> Error: Processing failed
        Generating --> Error: Generation failed

        Error --> Idle: Error dismissed
        Error --> Editing: Retry action
    ```

    ## API Endpoints

    ```mermaid
    sequenceDiagram
        participant Client as Next.js Client
        participant WS as WebSocket
        participant API as NestJS API
        participant Queue as Bull Queue
        participant Parser as Markdown Service
        participant Mermaid as Mermaid Plugin
        participant PDFGen as Puppeteer
        participant Storage as S3/R2

        Note over Client,Storage: PDF Export Flow with Mermaid

        Client->>API: POST /api/convert/pdf
        API->>API: Validate DTO (class-validator)
        API->>API: Check rate limit (Throttler)
        API->>Queue: Add job to queue
        Queue-->>API: Job ID
        API-->>Client: { jobId, status: 'queued' }

        Client->>WS: Subscribe (job-progress)

        Queue->>Parser: Process job
        Parser->>Parser: Parse Markdown
        Parser->>Mermaid: Detect & mark diagrams
        Mermaid-->>Parser: HTML with Mermaid blocks
        Parser->>WS: Progress: 30%
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'parsing', progress: 30 }

        Parser->>PDFGen: Generate PDF
        PDFGen->>PDFGen: Render HTML + Mermaid.js
        PDFGen->>PDFGen: Wait for diagrams
        PDFGen->>WS: Progress: 70%
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'rendering', progress: 70 }

        PDFGen->>Storage: Upload PDF
        Storage-->>PDFGen: File URL
        PDFGen->>WS: Complete
        WS-->>Client: { stage: 'complete', downloadUrl: '...' }

        Client->>Storage: Download PDF
    ```

    ### Endpoint Specifications

    | Endpoint                  | Method | Description              | Rate Limit |
    | ------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------ | ---------- |
    | `/api/convert/pdf`        | POST   | Queue PDF conversion job | 10/min     |
    | `/api/convert/pdf/:jobId` | GET    | Get job status/result    | 60/min     |
    | `/api/convert/html`       | POST   | Convert MD to HTML       | 20/min     |
    | `/api/upload`             | POST   | Upload .md file          | 5/min      |
    | `/api/health`             | GET    | Health check             | None       |
    | `/socket.io`              | WS     | Real-time job progress   | N/A        |

    ### NestJS DTO Examples

    ```typescript
    // apps/backend/src/modules/convert/dto/convert-pdf.dto.ts
    import { IsString, IsOptional, ValidateNested, IsEnum } from "class-validator";
    import { Type } from "class-transformer";

    class MarginsDto {
      @IsOptional() top?: string;
      @IsOptional() right?: string;
      @IsOptional() bottom?: string;
      @IsOptional() left?: string;
    }

    class PdfOptionsDto {
      @IsEnum(["a4", "letter", "legal"])
      @IsOptional()
      format?: "a4" | "letter" | "legal";

      @ValidateNested()
      @Type(() => MarginsDto)
      @IsOptional()
      margins?: MarginsDto;

      @IsOptional()
      showHeaderFooter?: boolean;
    }

    export class ConvertPdfDto {
      @IsString()
      markdown: string;

      @IsString()
      clientId: string;

      @ValidateNested()
      @Type(() => PdfOptionsDto)
      @IsOptional()
      options?: PdfOptionsDto;
    }
    ```

    ---

    ## Technology Decisions

    ### Why Separate NestJS Backend?

    - PDF generation is CPU-intensive → offload from Next.js
    - Independent scaling of PDF service
    - Bull queues for async processing with progress
    - WebSocket support for real-time status
    - Better separation of concerns
    - Easier to add auth, database later
    - Strong TypeScript support with decorators
    - Built-in validation, guards, interceptors

    ### Why Monorepo with Turborepo?

    - Shared types between frontend and backend
    - Single repository for easier maintenance
    - Parallel builds and caching
    - Consistent tooling across apps
    - Easier CI/CD setup

    ### Why CodeMirror 6 over Monaco?

    - Smaller bundle size (~100KB vs ~2MB)
    - Better mobile support
    - Excellent Markdown mode
    - Customizable and extensible
    - Lighter weight for this use case

    ### Why Puppeteer for PDF?

    - Highest fidelity output
    - Full CSS support
    - Mermaid.js executes natively (real browser)
    - JavaScript execution for dynamic content
    - Mature and well-maintained

    ### Why Bull + Redis for Queues?

    - Battle-tested job processing
    - Progress tracking built-in
    - Job retries and backoff
    - Dashboard available (Bull Board)
    - Persistent jobs survive restarts

    ### Why Mermaid.js?

    - Industry standard for diagrams in Markdown
    - Wide variety of diagram types (flowchart, sequence, gantt, etc.)
    - Active development and community
    - Theme support for dark/light mode
    - Works both client-side and in Puppeteer

    ---

    ## Risk Mitigation

    | Risk                       | Impact              | Mitigation                                 |
    | -------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
    | Puppeteer cold starts      | Slow first PDF      | Browser pool, warm instances               |
    | Large document performance | UI lag              | Virtual scrolling, Web Workers             |
    | API abuse                  | Resource exhaustion | Rate limiting, job queue                   |
    | XSS vulnerabilities        | Security breach     | Strict sanitization, CSP                   |
    | Mermaid syntax errors      | Broken preview      | Graceful error handling, fallback display  |
    | WebSocket disconnection    | Lost progress       | Reconnection logic, polling fallback       |
    | Redis downtime             | Queue failure       | Upstash with replication, fallback to sync |
    | High memory usage          | Backend crashes     | Browser pool limits, job cleanup           |

    ---

    ## Success Metrics

    | Metric              | Target       | Measurement       |
    | ------------------- | ------------ | ----------------- |
    | Page Load Time      | < 2s         | Lighthouse        |
    | PDF Generation Time | < 5s         | Job metrics       |
    | Error Rate          | < 0.1%       | Sentry            |
    | Uptime              | 99.9%        | Status monitoring |
    | Queue Throughput    | 100 jobs/min | Bull Board        |
    | User Satisfaction   | > 4.5/5      | Feedback form     |

    ---

    ## Future Enhancements (Post-Launch)

    1. **User Accounts** - Save documents to cloud
    2. **Collaboration** - Real-time multi-user editing (Yjs/CRDT)
    3. **Templates Library** - Pre-built document templates
    4. **Version History** - Document revision tracking
    5. **Image Upload** - Direct image embedding with S3
    6. **Public API** - API keys for integrations
    7. **Custom Mermaid Themes** - User-defined diagram styles
    8. **CLI Tool** - Command-line PDF generation
    9. **VS Code Extension** - Export from VS Code
    10. **Self-hosting** - Docker images for self-hosting

    ---

    ## Conclusion

    This project plan provides a structured approach to building a production-ready DryMDF application with:

    - **Next.js 14** frontend with CodeMirror 6 editor
    - **NestJS** backend with Bull queues and WebSocket
    - **Mermaid.js** support for diagrams
    - **Puppeteer** for high-quality PDF generation

    **Total Estimated Timeline: ~70 days (~14 weeks)**

    **Key Milestones:**

    - **Week 2**: Monorepo + basic frontend/backend
    - **Week 4**: Editor + Preview + Mermaid working
    - **Week 6**: PDF generation with queues
    - **Week 8**: All core features complete
    - **Week 10**: Performance and polish
    - **Week 12**: Testing complete
    - **Week 14**: Production launch

    ### Phase 1 — Deliver the desktop editor shell and first launch (MAC-09)

    - Use the Two Sheets icon from Identity for the app bundle and installer, with the separate wordmark on Welcome. Check the silhouette at 16, 32, and 128 pt in light and dark appearances. The Page Fold board is the design fallback if small-size legibility fails.
    - Use the Direction board’s system type, Monaco source text, blue selection, and thin dividers. At the 1080 × 690 reference size, place navigation on the left, Markdown in the center, and preview on the right. At 720 × 660, switch between Editor and Preview. The current [split pane](../apps/frontend/src/components/layout/split-pane.tsx) stacks both at narrow widths. Reuse CodeMirror and the existing preview components.
    - Implement Start, Recents, New Document, Open a File, and the editable sample with Start Over / Start Editing. Preserve Skip Setup and the existing draft on upgrade. Populate Recents from real opens. Workspace navigation becomes available with Phase 2.
    - **Pass when** first launch, skip, canceled Open, sample editing, and relaunch all lead to the intended document. Compare the packaged app with the light, dark, and compact boards. Verify keyboard access, focus return, and reduced motion and transparency.

    ### Phase 2 — Make workspaces reliable (MAC-06)

    - Implement Library → Create Workspace → Add Files → editor sidebar. Keep originals in place. Persist workspace membership, recent use, active file, and a stable ID per document. Migrate the existing single draft together with its local-image association. The [editor store](../apps/frontend/src/stores/editor-store.ts) currently persists one document and the [file bridge](../apps/desktop/documents.cjs) records one image root.
    - Track saved revisions and recoverable drafts separately. Make Save write the selected document. Keep its dirty indicator until that write succeeds. For external changes or a missing file, offer Keep Draft, Reload from Disk, or Locate File as applicable.
    - **Pass when** two files with the same name in different folders retain independent drafts and relative images after switching and quitting. Saving one changes only its original. Move one file and externally edit the other, then exercise each recovery action and verify the resulting disk contents.

    ### Phase 3 — Complete page setup, export, and settings (MAC-10)

    - Connect the designed paper size, orientation, and margin controls to both preview and print. Orientation is missing from the current [PDF options](../apps/frontend/src/types/pdf.ts). Retain existing color and numbering options. Show Generate Preview when empty and Refresh PDF when edits make the preview stale.
    - Deliver the format, filename, destination, progress, completion, and retry sheets. Reuse the native save dialog. The current [preload bridge](../apps/desktop/preload.cjs) returns a success flag. Give Show in Finder a reference to the completed export and retain the user’s choices for Export Again or Choose Folder.
    - Move the notification offer from onboarding to after the first successful PDF export. Put appearance, restore last session, notification preference, system settings access, and test alert in Settings. Honor earlier opt-in and opt-out choices.
    - **Pass when** changing orientation or margins produces matching preview and saved PDF pagination, HTML opens offline, and Markdown round-trips. Canceling leaves the destination untouched. A failed save supports retry to another folder. Show in Finder reveals the file actually written.

    ### Phase 4 — Connect and verify AI providers (MAC-07)

    - This work can begin after Phase 0 alongside the desktop UI. Build the settings screens for Ollama, LM Studio, and one hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Support model discovery, model selection, refresh, and a fixed-prompt connection test using no document content. Show where inference runs and distinguish unavailable server, empty model list, and authentication failure.
    - Route provider calls through typed Electron main-process operations. Keep local presets on loopback with downloaded local models, route cloud models through an explicit hosted choice, and require HTTPS for hosted requests. Keep keys in Keychain-backed storage scoped to provider and endpoint. Keep prompts, document contents, and secrets out of logs.
    - **Pass when** each local provider lists models, streams a response, and recovers after a server restart. Test one hosted endpoint with a supplied key. Check a packaged upgrade retains access to that endpoint’s key and switching endpoints cannot reuse it. Editing and export must work with AI off.

    ### Phase 5 — Ship context-aware chat and reviewed edits (MAC-08)

    - After Phases 2 and 4, use the editor’s right pane for chat. Start with the selection. Let the user explicitly add the active document or named workspace files. Show the prompt, provider, model, and included context. For hosted requests, show the Penpot **Review before sending** sheet with Cancel and Send Context before transmitting document text.
    - Stream the reply with Stop and Retry. Bind a suggestion to its source document, revision, and selected range. Show Original and Suggestion with Apply Edit and Discard. Apply one undoable CodeMirror change to the source draft. If the user switches files or changes the source, prevent applying to the wrong text and offer regeneration for a stale suggestion.
    - **Pass when** a request with a paragraph from Ridge walk.md and an explicitly added Gear list.md excludes Weather.md and the rest of Ridge walk.md. Canceling hosted review sends nothing. Stopping ignores late tokens. Discard leaves the draft intact, Apply updates the preview, and Undo restores the exact original. Check typing and switching files mid-stream.

    ### Phase 6 — Qualify and publish the redesigned app (MAC-05)

    - Build from the integrated revision after Phases 1–5. Compare the installed surfaces with the Penpot reference boards, including compact navigation and error recovery. Repeat the existing offline export fixture, upgrade a single-file draft, and run the workspace and provider acceptance cases from the packaged app.
    - **Pass when** a browser-downloaded DMG installs on a clean Apple Silicon Mac with Gatekeeper enabled, notification allow and deny paths have been observed, and the oldest claimed macOS version has passed. Publish those exact tested bytes, SHA-256, supported OS, and installation steps.

    The first usable redesign is Phase 1. Phase 2 makes it a multi-file editor, and Phase 5 completes the AI workflow. Keep cross-file writes, indexing, automatic tool execution, and additional hosted adapters outside this release.

    ## Multi-file workspaces and editor AI

    - **Workspaces:** Create a named workspace, then add Markdown files through the native picker. Show them in a sidebar with the active file and unsaved changes. Keep originals in place, save each file independently, and restore drafts after quitting. Handle missing or externally changed files before overwriting.
    - **AI settings:** Offer Ollama and LM Studio as local presets and one hosted OpenAI-compatible provider with an API key. Show where inference runs, list models, and offer a connection test with a fixed test prompt. Keep keys in Keychain-backed storage through Electron's main process, scoped to the provider and endpoint. Verify access across updates to the ad-hoc-signed DMG.
    - **Local routing:** Connect to loopback for local presets. Surface server unavailable, no models, and authentication errors. Treat Ollama cloud models as remote and require a hosted choice for them. Keep hosted requests on HTTPS and keep document data and keys out of logs.
    - **In-editor AI:** Default to the text selection when one exists. Offer explicit controls for the active file or named workspace files. Show the provider, model, and selected context before sending, with a clear disclosure for hosted requests. Stream responses with a Stop action. Present document edits as diffs with Apply and Discard and put applied edits on the editor's undo stack. If the source changed while AI was running, regenerate the suggestion against the new text.
    - **Launch scope:** Local AI downloads and runs through the user's chosen provider app. Editing and export work with AI disabled. Cross-file writes, workspace indexing, tool execution, and additional hosted adapters are deferred.

    Dossier provides a reference for provider selection, model discovery, endpoint-scoped keys, and connection testing. DryMDF's desktop bridge owns provider calls and only receives document context selected by the user.

    ## Build and install the test DMG

    Use Apple Silicon macOS, Node 22.12 or newer within the 22.x line, and the repository's pinned pnpm version. From the repository root, run:

    ```sh
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make
    ```

    Open `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg`, drag DryMDF into Applications, and launch it. If macOS blocks the first launch because it cannot verify the developer, try opening DryMDF first, then use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. [Apple's installation instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445)

    The build applies a local ad-hoc signature, verifies the app bundle, runs the packaged executable in headless mode, and writes a `.sha256` file next to the DMG. The direct download remains unnotarized.

    ## First-launch setup

    - The welcome flow introduces the editor, offline exports, and file access. It can be skipped or reopened with **Setup** in the desktop toolbar.
    - DryMDF receives file access through the macOS Open and Save dialogs. Relative images are read within the selected document's folder.
    - Export notifications start off. Users can opt in, send a test notification, and change their preference from **Setup**. macOS controls banner delivery under **System Settings → Notifications**. The editor reports export results in the app.
    - [x] Verify first launch, skip, relaunch, reopening Setup, and persisting the notification choice.
    - [x] Verify a test request and successful export route through the desktop bridge after opt-in. Verify opt-out stops export requests.
    - [ ] On a clean Mac, test notification delivery after allowing it and verify exports work after denying it.

    ### Release candidate with first-launch setup

    - **Installer:** SHA-256 is `8cadd1d7b4c601221dfb2bc724b813dcab58acc608b9c9beda857c67cc936374`. The previous ad-hoc signature enabled Hardened Runtime, causing macOS to reject the bundled Electron framework at startup. The rebuilt DMG uses per-file ad-hoc signing settings and checks the actual executable before creating the image.
    - **Setup:** Hidden-window tests verified onboarding, persistence, notification opt-in and opt-out, and export notification requests using a simulated notification service. Native banner delivery and the first-run system prompt still require visible testing.

    # DryMDF web history

    [[projects/drymdf/DryMDF|DryMDF]] · [[projects/drymdf/facts/activity|DryMDF activity]] · [[projects/drymdf/facts/roadmap|DryMDF roadmap]]

    ## Milestones

    - **2–3 February 2026.** Established the pnpm and Turborepo workspace, NestJS and Puppeteer backend, quality scripts, Next.js app, CodeMirror editor, and split preview.
    - **17–20 February 2026.** Added themed PDF export with progress tracking, Mermaid rendering, Markdown and PDF previews, page options and numbering, file upload, and the DryMDF brand and landing page.
    - **28 February 2026.** Added Redis and Docker configuration, deployment documentation, and Vercel configuration. PR #1 merged the development work and PR #2 merged the trackback into development.
    - **1–5 March 2026.** Development branch added CI and frontend/backend deployment workflows, followed by Node 20, Puppeteer, secrets/CORS, Vercel environment, and local dev-script fixes. PR #3 is open.

    ## GitHub activity

    | [#1 Development](https://github.com/ajay-mandal/DryMDF/pull/1) | Merged | 2026-02-28 |

    interface Props {

    export default function DesktopEditor({
      onOpen,
      onExport,
      onPreviewModeChange,
      pdfMode,
    }: Props) {
      const { filename, content, desktopDocumentId, setDesktopDocument } =
        useEditorStore();
      const [hasDraft, setHasDraft] = useState(
        () =>
          localStorage.getItem(screenKey) !== "empty" &&
          localStorage.getItem("drymdf-editor-storage") !== null,
      );
      const [editing, setEditing] = useState(
        () => hasDraft && localStorage.getItem(screenKey) !== "start",
      );
      const [sheet, setSheet] = useState<DesktopSheet>(() =>
        !hasDraft && !localStorage.getItem(setupKey) ? "welcome" : null,
      );
      const [pane, setPane] = useState<"editor" | "preview">("editor");
      const [recent, setRecent] = useState<RecentDocument[]>([]);
      const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
      const picker = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
      const heading = useRef<HTMLHeadingElement>(null);
      const hadDraftBeforeSample = useRef(false);
      const previous = useRef<ReturnType<typeof useEditorStore.getState> | null>(
        null,
      );
      const activeName =
        recent.find((item) => item.id === desktopDocumentId)?.name ??
        filename + ".md";

      useEffect(() => {
        let active = true;
        window.drymdfDesktop
          ?.listRecents()
          .then((items) => {
            if (active) setRecent(items);
          })
          .catch(() => toast.error("Couldn’t load recent documents."));
        return () => {
          active = false;
        };
      }, [editing, desktopDocumentId]);

      useEffect(() => {
        function shortcut(event: KeyboardEvent) {
          if (
            !event.metaKey ||
            event.altKey ||
            event.shiftKey ||
            busy ||
            document.querySelector(
              '[data-slot="dialog-content"][data-state="open"]',
            )
          )
            return;
          if (event.key === "o") {
            event.preventDefault();
            picker.current?.click();
          }
          if (event.key === ",") {
            event.preventDefault();
            setSheet("settings");
          }
        }
        window.addEventListener("keydown", shortcut);
        return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", shortcut);
      }, [busy]);

      function showEditor() {
        localStorage.setItem(setupKey, "complete");
        localStorage.setItem(screenKey, "editor");
        setHasDraft(true);
        setEditing(true);
        setPane("editor");
        setSheet(null);
      }

      function start() {
        localStorage.setItem(screenKey, hasDraft ? "start" : "empty");
        setEditing(false);
      }

      function mayReplace() {
        return (
          !hasDraft ||
          useEditorStore.getState().desktopDraftEdited === false ||
          window.confirm(
            "Replace your current local draft? Export it as Markdown first if you want to keep a copy.",
          )
        );
      }

      async function openFile(source: File | RecentDocument) {
        if (busy) return;
        if (
          !(source instanceof File) &&
          source.id === desktopDocumentId &&
          hasDraft
        ) {
          showEditor();
          return;
        }
        if (!mayReplace()) return;
        setBusy(true);
        try {
          if (source instanceof File) {
            if (!(await onOpen(source))) return;
          } else {
            const doc = await window.drymdfDesktop!.reopenMarkdown(source.id);
            setDesktopDocument(doc.content, getBaseFilename(doc.name), doc.id);
          }
          showEditor();
        } catch {
          toast.error("Couldn’t open this document. Use Open to locate the file.");
        } finally {

        }
      }

      function dismiss() {
        if (sheet === "welcome" || sheet === "sample")
          localStorage.setItem(setupKey, "complete");
        if (sheet === "sample") previous.current = null;
        setSheet(null);
        requestAnimationFrame(() => heading.current?.focus());
      }

      const chooseFile = () => picker.current?.click();
      const switchPane = () => setPane(pane === "editor" ? "preview" : "editor");
      const newDocument = () => {
        if (mayReplace()) {
          setDesktopDocument("", "Untitled");
          showEditor();
        }
      };
      return (
        <main className="mac-shell">
          <input
            hidden
            ref={picker}
            type="file"
            accept=".md,.markdown,text/markdown"
            onChange={(event) => {
              const file = event.target.files?.[0];
              event.target.value = "";
              if (file) void openFile(file);
            }}
          />
          <header className="mac-toolbar">
            <strong>DryMDF</strong>
            <div>
              {editing && (
                <button disabled={busy} onClick={chooseFile}>
                  <FolderOpen />
                  Open…
                </button>
              )}
              <DropdownMenu>
                <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
                  <button aria-label="View">
                    <PanelLeft />
                    View
                  </button>
                </DropdownMenuTrigger>
                <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
                  <DropdownMenuItem onSelect={start}>Recents</DropdownMenuItem>
                  <DropdownMenuItem onSelect={newDocument}>
                    New Document
                  </DropdownMenuItem>
                  <DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => setSheet("settings")}>
                    Settings…
                  </DropdownMenuItem>
                  <DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => setSheet("welcome")}>
                    Open Setup
                  </DropdownMenuItem>
                </DropdownMenuContent>
              </DropdownMenu>
              {editing && (
                <ExportDialog initialFilename={filename} onExport={onExport} />
              )}
            </div>
          </header>
          <div className="mac-body">
            <nav className="mac-sidebar" aria-label="Library">
              <small>Library</small>
