    - Implement Start, Recents, New Document, Open a File, and the editable sample with Start Over / Start Editing. Preserve Skip Setup and the existing draft on upgrade. Populate Recents from real opens. Workspace navigation becomes available with Phase 2.
    - **Pass when** first launch, skip, canceled Open, sample editing, and relaunch all lead to the intended document. Compare the packaged app with the light, dark, and compact boards. Verify keyboard access, focus return, and reduced motion and transparency.
    ## First-launch setup

    - The welcome flow introduces the editor, offline exports, and file access. It can be skipped or reopened with **Setup** in the desktop toolbar.
    - DryMDF receives file access through the macOS Open and Save dialogs. Relative images are read within the selected document's folder.
    - Export notifications start off. Users can opt in, send a test notification, and change their preference from **Setup**. macOS controls banner delivery under **System Settings → Notifications**. The editor reports export results in the app.
    - [x] Verify first launch, skip, relaunch, reopening Setup, and persisting the notification choice.
    - [x] Verify a test request and successful export route through the desktop bridge after opt-in. Verify opt-out stops export requests.
    - [ ] On a clean Mac, test notification delivery after allowing it and verify exports work after denying it.

    ## Milestone acceptance

    ### Internal beta

    - [x] A packaged Apple Silicon build opens directly into the editor.
    - [x] An offline multi-page Markdown fixture renders and exports with Mermaid, KaTeX, and a JavaScript code block. A separate PDF probe verifies page numbers.
    - [x] PDF preview and saved PDF agree on page count and pagination for the fixture.

    ### Release MVP

    - [x] Users can create and edit Markdown, open a local `.md` file, and save PDF, HTML, and Markdown to a chosen folder offline. Local images, Unicode filenames, and paths with spaces work.

        const fs = require("node:fs/promises");
        const os = require("node:os");
        const path = require("node:path");
        const { spawn } = require("node:child_process");
        const delay = (ms) => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
        const binary = process.argv[2];

        async function withApp(profile, inspect) {
          const app = spawn(binary, [
            "--user-data-dir=" + profile,
            "--remote-debugging-port=0",
          ], { stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "inherit"] });
          let socket;
          try {
            let target;
            for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {
              assert.equal(app.exitCode, null, "installed app quit early");
              try {
                const port = (await fs.readFile(path.join(profile, "DevToolsActivePort"), "utf8")).split("\n")[0];
                const targets = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/json/list`).then(r => r.json());
                target = targets.find(t => t.url === "drymdf://app/editor/");
                if (target) break;
              } catch {}
              await delay(100);
            }
            assert.ok(target, "installed editor target");
            socket = new WebSocket(target.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
            await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
              socket.addEventListener("open", resolve, { once: true });
              socket.addEventListener("error", reject, { once: true });
            });
            let nextId = 0;
            async function send(method, params = {}) {
              const id = ++nextId;
              const result = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
                const receive = ({data}) => {
                  const reply = JSON.parse(data);
                  if (reply.id !== id) return;
                  socket.removeEventListener("message", receive);
                  if (reply.error) reject(new Error(reply.error.message));
                  else resolve(reply.result);
                };
                socket.addEventListener("message", receive);
              });
              socket.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
              return result;
            }
            async function evaluate(expression) {
              const res = await send("Runtime.evaluate", { expression, returnByValue: true });
              if (res.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(res.exceptionDetails));
              return res.result.value;
            }
            async function wait(expression) {
              for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {
                if (await evaluate(`Boolean(${expression})`)) return;
                await delay(100);
              }
              throw new Error(expression + " " + await evaluate("document.body.innerText"));
            }
            await inspect({ evaluate, wait, send });
          } finally {
            socket?.close();
            if (app.exitCode === null) {
              const exited = new Promise(resolve => app.once("exit", resolve));
              app.kill();
              await exited;
            }
          }
        }

        async function main() {
          const profile = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "drymdf-mac09-installed-"));
          await withApp(profile, async ({ evaluate, wait, send }) => {
            const click = label => evaluate(`[...document.querySelectorAll("[role=dialog] button")].find(b=>b.innerText===${JSON.stringify(label)}).click()`);
            await wait('document.querySelector("[data-sheet=welcome]")');
            await click("Try the Sample");
            await wait('document.querySelector("[data-sheet=sample]")');
            await click("Start Editing");
            await wait('document.activeElement?.matches(".cm-content")');
            await send("Input.insertText", { text: "Installed test " });
            await wait('document.querySelector(".cm-content").innerText.includes("Installed test")');
            await wait('document.querySelector("[data-md-preview-pane]").innerText.includes("Installed test")');
            const printed = await send("Runtime.evaluate", {
              expression: 'window.drymdfDesktop.printPdf("<h1>DryMDF installed</h1>", {}).then(bytes => new TextDecoder().decode(bytes.slice(0,5)))',
              awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true,
            });
            assert.equal(printed.result.value, "%PDF-");
            assert.equal(await evaluate('localStorage.getItem("drymdf-desktop-setup-v1")'), "complete");
            await delay(400);
          });
          await withApp(profile, async ({ wait, evaluate }) => {
            await wait('document.querySelector(".cm-content")?.innerText.includes("Installed test")');
            assert.equal(await evaluate('!!document.querySelector("[data-sheet]")'), false);
          });
          console.log("PASS mounted DMG copy, first launch, sample editing, local PDF printing, and isolated-profile relaunch");
        }

        main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });

    This skill gives you the tools and permission to create design that earns to be called out-of-distribution craft: Whereas before, your design work would have been safe, timid and measured, you now approach every design task as an award-winning design director with impeccable understanding for what makes exceptional design work: production-grade code, peak creativity, a clear POV, deep understanding of the needs of the client and users, and exceptional craft.

    Core principles:
    - Go all out. No hedging, no shortcuts. The deliverable must be complete (except assets the user must provide).
    - Dream big and bold. Distinct, beautiful, outstanding and highly inspiring work.
    - Verify in bounded passes, not a loop, and the ceiling covers the whole cycle: screenshots, defect scans, micro-edits, and rebuilds alike. Build fully, inspect once with a batched round (desktop and mobile together on the web; the shipped device classes on a native platform), fix everything it shows in one batch, confirm with at most one more round, and stop polishing. Open-ended self-QA burns the user's money doing worse what the finish handoffs do better.

    ## Setup

    1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.codex/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
    2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
    3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

    **Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

    ## How to design

    - **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
    - **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
    - **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

    ## Modes

    The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

    - **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
    - **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
    - **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
    - **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

    Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

    ## Commands

    | Command | Category | Description | Reference |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
    | `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
    | `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
    | `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
    | `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
    | `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
    | `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
    | `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
    | `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
    | `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
    | `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
    | `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
    | `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
    | `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
    | `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
    | `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
    | `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
    | `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
    | `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
    | `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |

    | `optimize [target]` | Fix | Diagnose and fix UI performance | [reference/optimize.md](reference/optimize.md) |
    | `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, generate alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |

    Routing:

    - **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
    - **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
    - **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
    - **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
    - `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

    # $impeccable hooks

    Manage the **design detector hook** for the current project.

    The hook runs the impeccable design detector on direct file edits to design-relevant files (`.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.html`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.astro`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`, `.ts`, `.js`). Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot use a post-tool-use hook and push a short system reminder into the agent's context after the edit; findings get a correction prompt, pending issues get a re-nudge, and clean UI-ish files get a short ack unless quiet mode is on (`hook.quiet` in config). Plain `.ts` and `.js` files are still scanned, but stay quiet unless the detector finds something. Cursor uses `preToolUse` to block bad proposed writes before they land and stays silent when it allows a clean write. Grok Build fires the same PostToolUse scan to mark touched files, then surfaces findings on Stop `additionalContext`. Do not expect a Grok per-edit reminder: Grok discards that stdout.

    The detector rules run in two tiers. The per-edit hook surfaces only the immediate tier: mechanical, unambiguous problems worth interrupting an edit for, such as broken images, overflowing or clipped content, contrast and legibility failures, gradient text, glow shadows, and design-system drift. Everything else (copy cadence, palette and typography taste, layout rhythm) is deferred to a deep pass on the `Stop` hook event, which runs the full rule set over every UI file touched in the session and surfaces the remaining findings once, deduplicated against what the per-edit pass already reported. A session with nothing left to report stops silently. Set `hook.perEditRules` to `"all"` in `.impeccable/config.json` to restore the full rule set on every edit. The Stop deep pass is wired for Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Build, which dispatch a native `Stop` hook event. Cursor does not get one (its stop hook is not consistently dispatched; the pre-write gate covers it), and GitHub Copilot's stop-style events do not feed context back to the model, so they keep the full detector per edit. Grok also fires an observe-only Stop with `reason: "shutdown"` after `end_turn`; skip that one, scan only `end_turn`.

    Every hook is a mechanical pass. The reflexes no scanner catches live in [craft-floor.md](craft-floor.md), which the skill loads before it edits UI, so they apply whether or not a hook is wired. A session with no automatic hook gets one `MANUAL_DETECTOR_REQUIRED` directive from `impeccable context` asking for a single detector run at the end.

    This command toggles the hook **per project** by editing `.impeccable/config.json` (the unified Impeccable config; hook runtime settings live under its `hook` key, and shared detector ignores live under `detector`). Per-developer overrides, including the install consent decision (`hook.consent`) the CLI records, live in the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json`. Set `hook.enabled: false` to turn the hook off, `hook.quiet: true` to silence the clean/pending acks, or `hook.auditLog` to a file path for an NDJSON log. The legacy `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_DISABLED`, `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_QUIET`, and `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_LOG` env vars are still honored and override these config values when set.

    Declare server-side template extensions under **`detector.extensions`** when the project uses Blade, Twig, ERB, or Handlebars files; the hook skips them otherwise because they sit outside the built-in extension list. One entry per extension, `{ "ext": ".blade.php", "engine": "html" }`. `engine` picks the analyzer (`html` for markup templates, `text` for JS/TS/CSS-like files) and defaults to `html`. Match against the end of the filename, so double extensions like `.blade.php` and `.html.erb` work. Config only adds extensions; the built-in list always applies.

    Manual `npx impeccable detect` scans use the same project filter config by default: `detector.ignoreRules`, `detector.ignoreFiles`, `detector.ignoreValues`, and `detector.designSystem.enabled`. `hook.enabled` only controls automatic hook execution, not manual CLI scans. Use `npx impeccable detect --no-config ...` for a raw detector run that ignores project config/context. Use `npx impeccable ignores ...` for direct CLI CRUD on the same detector ignores.

    Supported harnesses: Claude Code (`.claude/settings.local.json` in the project, which is gitignored so the hook stays machine-local; a hook you move into the shared `settings.json` is honored in place too), Codex (`.codex/hooks.json` in the project), Cursor (`.cursor/hooks.json` in the project), Grok Build (`.grok/hooks/impeccable.json` in the project; requires `/hooks-trust` or `--trust`), and GitHub Copilot (`.github/hooks/impeccable.json` in the project, a team-shared committed file that both the Copilot CLI and the cloud agent read). For the Copilot CLI, repo-level hooks fire once `.github/hooks/impeccable.json` is committed to the repository's default branch.

    On **Cursor**, `preToolUse` checks proposed Write/Edit/Shell write content and denies only when the real detector finds an issue. The denial message is visible to the agent as the tool error, so the agent can reconsider before the bad write lands.

    ## Routing

    The first argument is the action. Defaults to `status`.

    | Action | What it does |
    |---|---|
    | `status` | Print current state, shared/local config paths, ignored rules / files / values, env override. |
    | `on` | Set `enabled: true` in `.impeccable/config.json`, record local hook consent as accepted, and install/repair provider hook manifests when the skill is installed. |
    | `off` | Set `enabled: false` in `.impeccable/config.json`. |
    | `ignore-rule <id>` | Append `<id>` to `detector.ignoreRules`; for `overused-font`, requires `--all-values`. Suppresses the rule across the whole project. |
    | `ignore-file <glob>` | Append `<glob>` to `detector.ignoreFiles`. Suppresses **every** rule for matching files. |
    | `ignore-value <id> <value> [--shared] [--reason "..."]` | Append a rule/value suppression to shared `.impeccable/config.json`. |
    | `ignore-value <id> <value> --local [--reason "..."]` | Append a private rule/value suppression to `.impeccable/config.local.json`. |
    | `ignore-value <id> "*" --file <glob> [--file <glob>...]` | Turn one rule off in matching files only, leaving it active everywhere else. Repeat `--file`, or use `--file=<glob>` / `--files=<glob>`. A bare `"*"` with no `--file` is refused: use `ignore-rule <id>` if you really mean project-wide. |
    | `reset` | Delete the project config, dedup cache, and Cursor pending queue, and remove the hook's entries from every provider manifest `on` installs, the committed Copilot file included (a team-shared `settings.json` that `on` never writes is never touched). |

    ## Flow

    1. Resolve the action from the user's argument. If no action was given, default to `status`.
    2. Invoke the admin script and pass the user's output through verbatim:

       ```bash
       .codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hooks <action> [args...]
       ```

    3. If `<action>` is `off`, follow up with a one-line note: "Done. New edits will not trigger the design hook in this project until you run `$impeccable hooks on`."
    4. If `<action>` is `on`, follow up with: "Done. The design hook will fire after the next Edit/Write on a UI file."
    5. If `<action>` is `ignore-value`, `ignore-file`, or `ignore-rule`, just print the script output. The default scope is shared `.impeccable/config.json`; add `--local` only when the user explicitly asks for a private exception.
    6. If `<action>` is `status`, just print the script output. Do not add commentary unless the user asked a follow-up question.

    ## Triage findings

    The hook itself never writes ignore config; every exception goes through `impeccable hooks`. Triage each finding into one of three outcomes:

    - **Real design problem**: fix it. Never add an ignore to skip a fix or to push a blocked write through.
    - **Confident false positive or sanctioned exception**: persist the narrowest ignore yourself and disclose it in your reply. The bar is evidence you can name: an intentional demo or fixture, documentation of bad design, literal or domain-appropriate motion (a ball that bounces), or a choice the user already confirmed. Put that evidence in `--reason` as `"<who decided: evidence>"`; write "user confirmed" only when the user actually did.
    - **Unsure**: leave the finding standing and ask the user in one line. Ask once; a one-line question costs less than the hook re-firing on every later edit.

    Self-serve stops at `ignore-value`. `ignore-file` and `ignore-rule` silence too much to add on your own judgment; ask the user first.

    Prefer the narrowest exception:

    - If the finding line shows an `ignore-value <rule> <value>` pair, pass it to `impeccable hooks ignore-value` with your `--reason`. This writes shared `.impeccable/config.json` by default.
    - For value-specific findings such as `overused-font` and `bounce-easing`, use `ignore-value` for the specific value. Do not use `ignore-rule overused-font` for a specific font.
    - If the finding has no value-specific command, such as `side-tab`, scope that one rule to the file: `ignore-value <id> "*" --file <path>`. Run `npx impeccable detect <path>` first to see what actually fires there.
    - Reach for `ignore-file <path>` only when the whole file is out of scope for design review: a fixture, a generated artifact, a deliberate slop demo. It silences every rule for that file permanently, including rules that have not been written yet. A real UI surface with one noisy rule wants the file-scoped value ignore above.
    - Use `ignore-rule <id>` only when the user asks to suppress that whole rule across the project. For broad overused-font suppression, use `ignore-rule overused-font --all-values` only when the user asks to ignore overused fonts generally.
    - Prefer config ignores (the commands above) by default; they keep suppressions in one reviewable place. Reach for an inline comment only when the waiver must travel with a single file that leaves the repo (a generated/exported standalone document, an emailed HTML file). The supported marker is `impeccable-disable <rule>` (whole file) or `impeccable-disable-line` / `impeccable-disable-next-line` (one line), in any comment syntax, with an optional reason after `:` or `--`. The detector honors it by default; `--no-inline-ignores` or `--no-config` bypasses it.

    Example value-specific exception:

    ```bash
    .codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hooks ignore-value overused-font Inter --shared --reason "User confirmed Inter is intentional"
    ```

    Example self-served exception, with the evidence named:

    ```bash
    .codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hooks ignore-value bounce-easing bounce-ball --shared --reason "Agent: literal ball-bounce animation, bounce easing is the subject"
    ```

    Example whole-rule font exception:

    ```bash
    .codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hooks ignore-rule overused-font --all-values --reason "User asked to ignore overused fonts generally"
    ```

    Example one-rule-in-one-file exception, for a file that is still worth reviewing
    for everything else:

    ```bash
    .codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hooks ignore-value design-system-font-size "*" --file "src/overlay/widget.js" --reason "Injected widget builds its own type scale; DESIGN.md's ramp describes the site"
    ```

    Example whole-file exception, for a file that is out of scope entirely:

    ```bash
    .codex/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hooks ignore-file "src/legacy/Card.tsx"
    ```

    ## Constraints

    - Never modify `.impeccable/config.json` or `.impeccable/config.local.json` by hand from this command. Always go through `impeccable hooks` so writes stay validated and the file shape stays consistent. One exception: `detector.extensions` has no admin action, so when the user asks to cover a template stack, edit that one field in `.impeccable/config.json` directly and leave the rest of the file untouched.
    - Do not edit the launcher or the binary behind `impeccable hook` and `impeccable hook-before-edit` from this flow. Those are skill plumbing.
    - Cursor can block a proposed write when the detector finds a real issue. Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot do not block the edit; they emit a post-edit reminder instead. Disabling stops both blocking and reminders.
    - The hook is bundled with the Impeccable skill and installed through project-local manifests: `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.github/hooks/impeccable.json`. On Codex, the user must approve the hook via `/hooks` the first time. On Cursor, confirm hooks are enabled under Settings -> Hooks. On GitHub Copilot, the CLI loads `.github/hooks/impeccable.json` once it is committed to the repository's default branch, and the cloud agent reads it from the repo directly.

    ## Failure modes

    - If `.impeccable/config.json` or `.impeccable/config.local.json` is unreadable or malformed, the hook ignores that file and uses the remaining valid config/defaults. `impeccable hooks status` will show malformed files as ignored.
    - If the user asks to "disable the hook" globally, lead with `$impeccable hooks off` (persistent for this project; writes `hook.enabled: false` to config). The legacy `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_DISABLED=1` env var also works as a one-shot override that follows the shell.

    const { randomUUID } = require("node:crypto");
    const { app, BrowserWindow, dialog } = require("electron");
    const {
      readFile,
      realpath,
      rename,
      rm,
      stat,
      writeFile,
    } = require("node:fs/promises");
    const {
      basename,
      dirname,
      extname,
      isAbsolute,
      join,
      relative,
      resolve,
      sep,
    } = require("node:path");

    const imageTypes = {
      ".gif": "image/gif",
      ".jpeg": "image/jpeg",
      ".jpg": "image/jpeg",
      ".png": "image/png",
      ".webp": "image/webp",
    };
    const exportTypes = { ".md": "Markdown", ".html": "HTML", ".pdf": "PDF" };

    function documentStatePath() {
      return join(app.getPath("userData"), "document-folder.json");
    }

    async function replaceFile(path, data) {
      const temporary = join(dirname(path), `.drymdf-${randomUUID()}`);
      try {
        await writeFile(temporary, data, { flag: "wx" });
        await rename(temporary, path);
      } finally {
        await rm(temporary, { force: true });
      }
    }

    async function rememberedDocuments() {
      try {
        const state = JSON.parse(await readFile(documentStatePath(), "utf8"));
        // The single-file build remembered only the last document's image root.
        return state.documents ?? [state];
      } catch (error) {
        if (error.code === "ENOENT") return [];
        throw error;
      }
    }

    async function listRecents() {
      return (await rememberedDocuments())
        .filter((doc) => doc.path)
        .map(({ id, path }) => ({
          id,
          name: basename(path),
          folder: basename(dirname(path)),
        }));
    }

    let pendingOpen = Promise.resolve();

    function openMarkdown(path) {
      const next = pendingOpen.then(() => rememberOpenedFile(path));
      pendingOpen = next.catch(() => {});
      return next;
    }

    async function chooseMarkdown(sender) {
      const { canceled, filePaths } = await dialog.showOpenDialog(
        BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(sender),
        {
          title: "Open a Markdown file",
          properties: ["openFile"],
          filters: [{ name: "Markdown", extensions: ["md", "markdown"] }],
        },
      );
      if (canceled || !filePaths[0]) return null;
      return openMarkdown(filePaths[0]);
    }

    async function reopenMarkdown(id) {
      const entry = (await rememberedDocuments()).find((doc) => doc.id === id);
      if (!entry?.path) throw new Error("Choose the file again with Open.");
      return openMarkdown(entry.path);
    }

    async function rememberOpenedFile(path) {
      if (
        typeof path !== "string" ||
        !isAbsolute(path) ||
        !/\.(md|markdown)$/i.test(path)
      ) {
        throw new Error("Choose a .md or .markdown file.");
      }
      const root = await realpath(dirname(path));
      const content = await readFile(path, "utf8");
      const documents = await rememberedDocuments();
      const id = documents.find((doc) => doc.path === path)?.id ?? randomUUID();
      const recent = [
        { id, root, path },
        ...documents.filter((doc) => doc.id !== id),
      ].slice(0, 30);
      await replaceFile(documentStatePath(), JSON.stringify({ documents: recent }));
      return { id, content, name: basename(path) };
    }

    async function readImage(id, source) {
      if (typeof id !== "string" || typeof source !== "string") return null;
      try {
        const state = (await rememberedDocuments()).find((doc) => doc.id === id);
        if (!state) return null;
        const path = decodeURIComponent(source.split(/[?#]/, 1)[0]);
        if (!path || isAbsolute(path) || /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i.test(path))
          return null;
        const image = await realpath(resolve(state.root, path));
        const withinRoot = relative(state.root, image);
        if (
          !withinRoot ||
          withinRoot === ".." ||
          withinRoot.startsWith(".." + sep) ||
          isAbsolute(withinRoot)
        ) {
          return null;
        }
        const mime = imageTypes[extname(image).toLowerCase()];
        if (!mime) return null;
        const entry = await stat(image);
        if (!entry.isFile() || entry.size > 20 * 1024 * 1024) return null;
        return `data:${mime};base64,${(await readFile(image)).toString("base64")}`;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }

    async function saveDocument(sender, filename, extension, data) {
      if (
        !Object.hasOwn(exportTypes, extension) ||
        typeof filename !== "string" ||
        !filename ||
        filename !== basename(filename) ||
        filename.includes("\0")
      ) {
        throw new Error("Enter a valid export filename.");
      }
      const name = filename.toLowerCase().endsWith(extension)
        ? filename
        : filename + extension;
      const { canceled, filePath } = await dialog.showSaveDialog(
        BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(sender),
        {
          defaultPath: name,
          filters: [
            { name: exportTypes[extension], extensions: [extension.slice(1)] },
          ],
        },
      );
      if (canceled || !filePath) return false;
      await replaceFile(
        filePath,
        typeof data === "string" ? data : Buffer.from(data),
      );
      return true;
    }

    module.exports = {
      chooseMarkdown,
      openMarkdown,
      listRecents,
      reopenMarkdown,
      readImage,
      saveDocument,
    };

    # Vercel React Best Practices

    Comprehensive performance optimization guide for React and Next.js applications, maintained by Vercel. Contains 70 rules across 8 categories, prioritized by impact to guide automated refactoring and code generation.

    ## When to Apply

    Reference these guidelines when:
    - Writing new React components or Next.js pages
    - Implementing data fetching (client or server-side)
    - Reviewing code for performance issues
    - Refactoring existing React/Next.js code
    - Optimizing bundle size or load times

    ## Rule Categories by Priority

    | Priority | Category | Impact | Prefix |
    |----------|----------|--------|--------|
    | 1 | Eliminating Waterfalls | CRITICAL | `async-` |
    | 2 | Bundle Size Optimization | CRITICAL | `bundle-` |
    | 3 | Server-Side Performance | HIGH | `server-` |
    | 4 | Client-Side Data Fetching | MEDIUM-HIGH | `client-` |
    | 5 | Re-render Optimization | MEDIUM | `rerender-` |
    | 6 | Rendering Performance | MEDIUM | `rendering-` |
    | 7 | JavaScript Performance | LOW-MEDIUM | `js-` |
    | 8 | Advanced Patterns | LOW | `advanced-` |

    ## Quick Reference

    ### 1. Eliminating Waterfalls (CRITICAL)

    - `async-cheap-condition-before-await` - Check cheap sync conditions before awaiting flags or remote values
    - `async-defer-await` - Move await into branches where actually used
    - `async-parallel` - Use Promise.all() for independent operations
    - `async-dependencies` - Use better-all for partial dependencies
    - `async-api-routes` - Start promises early, await late in API routes
    - `async-suspense-boundaries` - Use Suspense to stream content

    ### 2. Bundle Size Optimization (CRITICAL)

    - `bundle-barrel-imports` - Import directly, avoid barrel files
    - `bundle-analyzable-paths` - Prefer statically analyzable import and file-system paths to avoid broad bundles and traces
    - `bundle-dynamic-imports` - Use next/dynamic for heavy components
    - `bundle-defer-third-party` - Load analytics/logging after hydration
    - `bundle-conditional` - Load modules only when feature is activated
    - `bundle-preload` - Preload on hover/focus for perceived speed

    ### 3. Server-Side Performance (HIGH)

    - `server-auth-actions` - Authenticate server actions like API routes
    - `server-cache-react` - Use React.cache() for per-request deduplication
    - `server-cache-lru` - Use LRU cache for cross-request caching
    - `server-dedup-props` - Avoid duplicate serialization in RSC props
    - `server-hoist-static-io` - Hoist static I/O (fonts, logos) to module level
    - `server-no-shared-module-state` - Avoid module-level mutable request state in RSC/SSR
    - `server-serialization` - Minimize data passed to client components

    interface EditorStore {
      content: string;
      filename: string;
      desktopDocumentId?: string;
      desktopDraftEdited?: boolean;
      settings: EditorSettings;

      setContent: (content: string) => void;
      setFilename: (filename: string) => void;
      setDesktopDocument: (content: string, filename: string, id?: string) => void;
      updateSettings: (settings: Partial<EditorSettings>) => void;
      resetContent: () => void;
    }

    const defaultSettings: EditorSettings = {
      theme: "light",
      fontSize: 14,
      lineHeight: 1.6,
      wordWrap: true,
      showLineNumbers: true,
      autoSave: true,
    };

    const defaultContent = `# Welcome to DryMDF

    Write your **Markdown** here and see it rendered in real-time!

    ## Features

    - ✨ Live preview
    - 📄 Export to PDF
    - 🎨 Mermaid diagram support
    - 💾 Auto-save
    - 🌙 Dark mode

    ## Example Code

    \`\`\`typescript

    }
    \`\`\`

    ## Mermaid Diagram

    \`\`\`mermaid
    graph TD

        B -->|Yes| C[Great!]
        B -->|No| D[Debug]
        D --> A
    \`\`\`

    Start typing to begin!
    `;

    const defaultFilename = "document";

    export const useEditorStore = create<EditorStore>()(
      persist(
        (set) => ({
          content: defaultContent,
          filename: defaultFilename,
          settings: defaultSettings,

          setContent: (content) =>
            set(
              process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_DRYMDF_DESKTOP === "1"
                ? { content, desktopDraftEdited: true }
                : { content },
            ),

          setFilename: (filename) => set({ filename }),
          setDesktopDocument: (content, filename, desktopDocumentId) =>
            set({
              content,
              filename,
              desktopDocumentId,
              desktopDraftEdited: false,
            }),

          updateSettings: (newSettings) =>
            set((state) => ({
              settings: { ...state.settings, ...newSettings },
            })),

          resetContent: () =>
            set({ content: defaultContent, desktopDocumentId: undefined }),
        }),
        {
          name: "drymdf-editor-storage",
          partialize: (state) => ({
            content: state.content,
            filename: state.filename,
            desktopDocumentId: state.desktopDocumentId,
            desktopDraftEdited: state.desktopDraftEdited,
            settings: state.settings,
          }),
        },
      ),
    );

    import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
    import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
    import { useEditorStore } from "@/stores/editor-store";
    import { useExportStore } from "@/stores/export-store";
    import { isDesktop } from "@/lib/desktop";
    import type { PdfOptions } from "@/types/pdf";
    import { toast } from "sonner";
    import { MarkdownPreviewPane } from "./markdown-preview-pane";
    import { PdfPreviewPane } from "./pdf-preview-pane";

    interface MarkdownPreviewProps {
      desktopShell?: boolean;
      sampleContent?: string;
      onPreviewModeChange?: (mode: "markdown" | "pdf") => void;
    }

    interface PdfPreviewRequest {
      id: number;
      content: string;
      documentId?: string;
      options: PdfOptions;
    }

    function clonePdfOptions(options: PdfOptions): PdfOptions {
      return {
        ...options,
        margins: options.margins ? { ...options.margins } : undefined,
      };
    }

    export function MarkdownPreview({
      onPreviewModeChange,
      desktopShell,
      sampleContent,
    }: MarkdownPreviewProps) {
      const { content: draft, desktopDocumentId } = useEditorStore();
      const content = sampleContent ?? draft;
      const { pdfOptions, updatePdfOptions } = useExportStore();
      const [mode, setPreviewMode] = useState<"markdown" | "pdf">("markdown");
      const previewMode = sampleContent === undefined ? mode : "markdown";
      const [pdfPreviewRequest, setPdfPreviewRequest] =
        useState<PdfPreviewRequest | null>(null);

      useEffect(() => {
        onPreviewModeChange?.(previewMode);
      }, [previewMode, onPreviewModeChange]);

      const isPdfPreviewOutdated =
        previewMode === "pdf" &&
        !!pdfPreviewRequest &&
        (content !== pdfPreviewRequest.content ||
          desktopDocumentId !== pdfPreviewRequest.documentId);

      useEffect(() => {
        if (previewMode !== "pdf") {
          return;
        }

        Promise.resolve().then(() => {
          setPdfPreviewRequest((currentRequest) => {
            if (!currentRequest) {
              return currentRequest;
            }

            const isMarkdownChanged =
              content !== currentRequest.content ||
              desktopDocumentId !== currentRequest.documentId;
            if (isMarkdownChanged) {
              return currentRequest;
            }

            const areOptionsChanged =
              JSON.stringify(pdfOptions) !== JSON.stringify(currentRequest.options);

            if (!areOptionsChanged) {
              return currentRequest;
            }

            toast.success("PDF settings updated", {
              id: "pdf-preview-settings",
              duration: 1200,
            });

            return {
              id: Date.now(),
              content: currentRequest.content,
              documentId: currentRequest.documentId,
              options: clonePdfOptions(pdfOptions),
            };
          });
        });
      }, [previewMode, pdfOptions, content, desktopDocumentId]);

      const handlePdfPreviewClick = () => {
        setPreviewMode("pdf");
        setPdfPreviewRequest({
          id: Date.now(),
          content,
          documentId: desktopDocumentId,
          options: clonePdfOptions(pdfOptions),
        });
      };

      return (
        <div className="h-full min-h-0 w-full flex flex-col overflow-hidden bg-slate-100 dark:bg-slate-900">
          <div className="md-toolbar border-b border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 px-3 sm:px-4 py-2">
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-3">
              <div
                className={
                  desktopShell && !isPdfPreviewOutdated
                    ? "hidden"
                    : "flex items-center gap-2 min-w-0"
                }
              >
                <div className="h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-blue-500" />
                <span className="text-xs font-medium text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 truncate">
                  {previewMode === "pdf" ? "PDF Preview" : "Markdown Preview"}
                </span>
                {isPdfPreviewOutdated && (
                  <span className="text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wide text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-400 whitespace-nowrap">
                    Outdated preview · re-click PDF Preview
                  </span>
                )}
              </div>

              <div className="md-modes flex items-center gap-1 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-md p-1 shrink-0">
                <Button
                  aria-pressed={previewMode === "markdown"}
                  variant={previewMode === "markdown" ? "secondary" : "ghost"}
                  size="xs"
                  onClick={() => setPreviewMode("markdown")}
                >
                  {desktopShell ? "Markdown" : "MD Preview"}
                </Button>
                <Button
                  aria-pressed={previewMode === "pdf"}
                  variant={previewMode === "pdf" ? "secondary" : "ghost"}
                  size="xs"
                  onClick={handlePdfPreviewClick}
                >
                  {desktopShell ? "PDF" : "PDF Preview"}
                </Button>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div className="flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden">
            {previewMode === "pdf" ? (
              <PdfPreviewPane
                request={
                  isDesktop() && isPdfPreviewOutdated ? null : pdfPreviewRequest
                }
                currentPdfOptions={pdfOptions}
                updatePdfOptions={updatePdfOptions}
              />
            ) : (
              <MarkdownPreviewPane content={content} />
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
      );
    }

            id: entry.id,
            name: basename(entry.path),
            folder: basename(entry.root),
            ...snapshot,
          };
        }

        async function selectedMarkdown(sender, title, multiple = false) {
          const { canceled, filePaths } = await dialog.showOpenDialog(
            BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(sender),
            {
              title,
              properties: multiple ? ["openFile", "multiSelections"] : ["openFile"],
              filters: [{ name: "Markdown", extensions: ["md", "markdown"] }],
            },
          );
          return canceled ? [] : filePaths;
        }

        function openMarkdown(path) {
          return registerMarkdown([path]).then(([document]) => document);
        }

        async function chooseMarkdown(sender) {
          const [path] = await selectedMarkdown(sender, "Open a Markdown file");
          return path ? openMarkdown(path) : null;
        }

        async function chooseWorkspaceFiles(sender) {
          const paths = await selectedMarkdown(sender, "Add Markdown files", true);
          return paths.length ? registerMarkdown(paths) : [];
        }

        async function reopenMarkdown(id) {
          const entry = (await rememberedDocuments()).find((doc) => doc.id === id);
          if (!entry?.path) throw new Error("Choose the file again with Open.");
          return openMarkdown(entry.path);
        }

        async function markdownPath(path) {
          if (
            typeof path !== "string" ||
            !isAbsolute(path) ||
            !/\\.(md|markdown)$/i.test(path)
          ) {
            throw new Error("Choose a .md or .markdown file.");
          }
          // Canonical paths keep a file's ID stable across repeated selection.
          const canonical = await realpath(path);
          if (!/\\.(md|markdown)$/i.test(canonical)) {
            throw new Error("Choose a .md or .markdown file.");
          }
          return canonical;
        }

        function registerMarkdown(paths) {
          return mutateDocuments(async () => {
            const canonical = [...new Set(await Promise.all(paths.map(markdownPath)))];
            const [documents, snapshots] = await Promise.all([
              rememberedDocuments(),
              Promise.all(canonical.map(readMarkdown)),
            ]);
            const opened = canonical.map((path) => ({
              id: documents.find((doc) => doc.path === path)?.id ?? randomUUID(),
              root: dirname(path),
              path,
            }));
            const openedIds = new Set(opened.map(({ id }) => id));
            await writeDocuments([
              ...opened,
              ...documents.filter((doc) => !openedIds.has(doc.id)),
            ]);
            return opened.map((entry, index) => describeDocument(entry, snapshots[index]));
          });
        }

        async function checkWorkspaceFile(_sender, id) {
          const entry = (await rememberedDocuments()).find((doc) => doc.id === id);
          if (!entry?.path) return { status: "missing" };
          try {
            return { status: "available", document: describeDocument(entry, await readMarkdown(entry.path)) };
          } catch (error) {
            if (error.code === "ENOENT" || error.code === "ENOTDIR") {
              return { status: "missing" };
            }
            throw error;
          }
        }

        async function locateWorkspaceFile(sender, id) {
          const [selected] = await selectedMarkdown(sender, "Locate Markdown file");
          if (!selected) return null;
          return mutateDocuments(async () => {
            const path = await markdownPath(selected);
            const documents = await rememberedDocuments();
            if (!documents.some((doc) => doc.id === id)) {
              throw new Error("This document is no longer registered.");
            }
            if (documents.some((doc) => doc.path === path && doc.id !== id)) {
              throw new Error("That file is already registered. Choose the document’s new location.");
            }
            const snapshot = await readMarkdown(path);
            const entry = { id, path, root: dirname(path) };
            await writeDocuments([entry, ...documents.filter((doc) => doc.id !== id)]);
            return describeDocument(entry, snapshot);
          });
        }

        function saveWorkspaceFile(sender, id, expectedRevision, content) {
          if (typeof expectedRevision !== "string" || typeof content !== "string") {
            throw new Error("Invalid save request.");
          }

          return mutateDocuments(async () => {
            const documents = await rememberedDocuments();
            const entry = documents.find((doc) => doc.id === id);
            const disk = await checkWorkspaceFile(sender, id);
            if (disk.status === "missing" || disk.document.revision !== expectedRevision) {
              return disk;
            }
            const bytes = Buffer.from(content, "utf8");
            // Keep existing permissions and check again immediately before replacing.
            const stale = Symbol("stale document");
            let changed;
            try {
              const mode = (await stat(entry.path)).mode & 0o777;
              await replaceFile(entry.path, bytes, {
                mode,
                beforeRename: async () => {
                  changed = await checkWorkspaceFile(sender, id);
                  if (changed.status === "missing" || changed.document.revision !== expectedRevision) {
                    throw stale;
                  }
                },
              });
            } catch (error) {
              if (error === stale) return changed;
              if (error.code === "ENOENT" || error.code === "ENOTDIR") {
                return { status: "missing" };
              }
              throw error;
            }
            return { status: "saved", revision: revision(bytes) };
          });
        }

        "use client";

        import { FileText, Folder, FolderPlus } from "lucide-react";
        import { useState } from "react";
        import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
        import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogTitle } from "@/components/ui/dialog";
        import type { DesktopDocument, DiskDocument } from "@/lib/desktop";
        import type { Workspace, WorkspaceFile } from "@/stores/editor-store";

        interface LibraryProps {
          workspaces: Workspace[];
          onCreate: () => void;
          onOpen: (id: string) => void;
        }

        export function WorkspaceLibrary({ workspaces, onCreate, onOpen }: LibraryProps) {
          const sorted = [...workspaces].sort((left, right) => right.openedAt - left.openedAt);
          return (
            <section className="mac-page" aria-labelledby="mac-workspaces-title">
              <div className="mac-page-heading">
                <div>
                  <h1 id="mac-workspaces-title">Workspaces</h1>
                  <p>Organize related Markdown files on this Mac.</p>
                </div>
                <Button className="mac-primary" onClick={onCreate}><FolderPlus /> Create Workspace</Button>
              </div>
              {sorted.length ? (
                <ul className="mac-library-list" aria-label="Workspaces">
                  {sorted.map((workspace) => (
                    <li key={workspace.id}>
                      <button onClick={() => onOpen(workspace.id)}>
                        <Folder />
                        <strong>{workspace.name}</strong>
                        <span>{workspace.fileIds.length} {workspace.fileIds.length === 1 ? "file" : "files"}</span>
                        <time dateTime={new Date(workspace.openedAt).toISOString()}>
                          {new Date(workspace.openedAt).toLocaleDateString(undefined, { month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" })}
                        </time>
                      </button>
                    </li>
                  ))}
                </ul>
              ) : (
                <p className="mac-workspace-empty">Create a workspace to open a group of files together.</p>
              )}
            </section>
          );
        }

        export function CreateWorkspaceDialog({ onClose, onCreate }: {
          onClose: () => void;
          onCreate: (name: string, files: DesktopDocument[]) => void;
        }) {
          const [name, setName] = useState("");
          const [files, setFiles] = useState<DesktopDocument[]>([]);
          const [picking, setPicking] = useState(false);
          const [error, setError] = useState("");

          async function chooseFiles() {
            setPicking(true);
            setError("");
            try {
              const selected = await window.drymdfDesktop!.chooseWorkspaceFiles();
              setFiles((previous) => [...new Map([...previous, ...selected].map((file) => [file.id, file])).values()]);
            } catch {
              setError("Couldn’t add the selected files. Choose readable Markdown files and try again.");
            } finally {
              setPicking(false);
            }
          }

          return (
            <Dialog open onOpenChange={(open) => { if (!open && !picking) onClose(); }}>
              <DialogContent className="mac-sheet mac-workspace-sheet" showCloseButton={false}>
                <DialogTitle>Create Workspace</DialogTitle>
                <DialogDescription>Group Markdown files so you can open them together.</DialogDescription>
                <form onSubmit={(event) => {
                  event.preventDefault();
                  if (name.trim() && !picking) onCreate(name.trim(), files);
                }}>
                  <label className="mac-workspace-name">
                    Workspace name
                    <input value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)} required maxLength={100} />
                  </label>
                  <div className="mac-workspace-add">
                    <h3>Files in this workspace</h3>
                    <Button type="button" variant="outline" disabled={picking} onClick={() => void chooseFiles()}>Add Files…</Button>
                  </div>
                  {files.length > 0 && <ul className="mac-picked-files">
                    {files.map((file) => <li key={file.id}><FileText /><span>{file.name}<small>{file.folder}</small></span></li>)}
                  </ul>}
                  {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
                  <p>Files stay in their original locations.</p>
                  <footer>
                    <Button type="button" variant="outline" disabled={picking} onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
                    <Button type="submit" disabled={!name.trim() || picking}>Create</Button>
                  </footer>
                </form>
              </DialogContent>
            </Dialog>
          );
        }

        export function WorkspaceRecoveryDialog({ file, disk, busy, onKeep, onReload, onLocate }: {
          file: WorkspaceFile;
          disk: DiskDocument;
          busy: boolean;
          onKeep: () => void;
          onReload: () => void;
          onLocate: () => void;
        }) {
          const available = disk.status === "available";
          return (
            <Dialog open onOpenChange={(open) => { if (!open && !busy) onKeep(); }}>
              <DialogContent className="mac-sheet mac-workspace-sheet" showCloseButton={false}>
                <DialogTitle>{file.name} {available ? "changed on disk" : "couldn’t be found"}</DialogTitle>
                <DialogDescription>
                  {available ? "Choose which version to keep editing. Keep Draft leaves the disk file as it is until you save." : "Your draft is safe. Locate the original file to save changes back to it."}
                </DialogDescription>
                {available && (
                  <div className="mac-recovery-versions">
                    <section><h3>Draft in DryMDF</h3><pre>{file.content.slice(0, 360) || "(Empty document)"}</pre></section>
                    <section><h3>On disk</h3><pre>{disk.document.content.slice(0, 360) || "(Empty document)"}</pre></section>
                  </div>
                )}
                <footer>
                  <Button variant="outline" disabled={busy} onClick={onLocate}>Locate File…</Button>
                  {available && <Button variant="outline" disabled={busy} onClick={onReload}>Reload from Disk</Button>}
                  <Button disabled={busy} onClick={onKeep}>Keep Draft</Button>
                </footer>
              </DialogContent>
            </Dialog>
          );
        }

        type Recovery = { id: string; disk: DiskDocument };

        export function useWorkspaceFiles(active: boolean, documentId?: string) {
          const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
          const [recovery, setRecovery] = useState<Recovery>();
          const inFlight = useRef(false);
          const checking = useRef(0);

          async function run(operation: () => Promise<void>, error: string) {
            if (inFlight.current) return;
            inFlight.current = true;
            checking.current++;
            setBusy(true);
            try {
              await operation();
            } catch (cause) {
              toast.error(error, {
                description: cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : undefined,
              });
            } finally {
              inFlight.current = false;
              setBusy(false);
            }
          }

          function activeFile() {
            const state = useEditorStore.getState();
            return state.workspaceId && state.desktopDocumentId
              ? state.workspaceFiles[state.desktopDocumentId]
              : undefined;
          }

          const check = useEffectEvent(async () => {
            if (!active || inFlight.current || recovery || !documentId) return;
            const file = activeFile();
            const api = window.drymdfDesktop;
            if (!file || !api) return;
            const request = ++checking.current;
            try {
              const disk = await api.checkWorkspaceFile(file.id);
              if (request !== checking.current || activeFile()?.id !== file.id) return;
              if (disk.status === "missing" || disk.document.revision !== file.revision) {
                setRecovery({ id: file.id, disk });
              }
            } catch {
              if (request === checking.current) {
                toast.error("Couldn’t check the file on disk.", { id: "workspace-file-check" });
              }
            }
          });

          useEffect(() => {
            const onFocus = () => void check();
            onFocus();
            window.addEventListener("focus", onFocus);
            return () => {
              checking.current++;
              window.removeEventListener("focus", onFocus);
            };
          }, [active, documentId]);

          function save() {
            const file = activeFile();
            if (!file || recovery) return;
            void run(async () => {
              const api = window.drymdfDesktop!;
              const result = file.revision
                ? await api.saveWorkspaceFile(file.id, file.revision, file.content)
                : await api.checkWorkspaceFile(file.id);
              if (result.status === "saved") {
                // Keep edits made while the write was in flight in the recoverable draft.
                useEditorStore.getState().updateWorkspaceFile(file.id, {
                  revision: result.revision,
                  savedContent: file.content,
                });
                toast.success("Saved to disk", { id: "workspace-save" });
              } else {
                setRecovery({ id: file.id, disk: result });
              }
            }, "Couldn’t save the file.");
          }

          function chooseFiles(onChoose: (files: DesktopDocument[]) => void, multiple: boolean) {
            void run(async () => {
              const api = window.drymdfDesktop!;
              if (multiple) {
                const files = await api.chooseWorkspaceFiles();
                if (files.length) onChoose(files);
              } else {
                const file = await api.chooseMarkdown();
                if (file) onChoose([file]);
              }
            }, "Couldn’t add the selected files.");
          }

          function keep() {
            if (!recovery) return;
            if (recovery.disk.status === "available") {
              const { revision, content } = recovery.disk.document;
              useEditorStore.getState().updateWorkspaceFile(recovery.id, {
                revision,
                savedContent: content,
              });
            }
            setRecovery(undefined);
          }

          function reload() {
            if (recovery?.disk.status !== "available") return;
            const { id, disk } = recovery;
            void run(async () => {
              const latest = await window.drymdfDesktop!.checkWorkspaceFile(id);
              if (latest.status === "missing" || latest.document.revision !== disk.document.revision) {
                setRecovery({ id, disk: latest });
                return;
              }
              useEditorStore.getState().updateWorkspaceFile(id, {
                ...latest.document,
                savedContent: latest.document.content,
              });
              setRecovery(undefined);
            }, "Couldn’t reload the file.");
          }

          function locate() {
            if (!recovery) return;
            const { id } = recovery;
            void run(async () => {
              const found = await window.drymdfDesktop!.locateWorkspaceFile(id);
              if (!found) return;
              const state = useEditorStore.getState();
              const file = state.workspaceFiles[id];
              state.updateWorkspaceFile(id, {
                name: found.name,
                folder: found.folder,
                locationVersion: (file.locationVersion ?? 0) + 1,
              });
              if (found.revision === file.revision) {
                setRecovery(undefined);
              } else {
                setRecovery({ id, disk: { status: "available", document: found } });
              }
            }, "Couldn’t locate the file.");
          }

          return { busy, recovery, save, chooseFiles, keep, reload, locate };
        }

            </DropdownMenuTrigger>
            <DropdownMenuContent align="end" className="w-56">
              <DropdownMenuLabel className="text-xs text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400">
                Page Numbering
              </DropdownMenuLabel>
              <DropdownMenuSeparator />
              <DropdownMenuLabel className="text-xs text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400">
                Status
              </DropdownMenuLabel>
              <DropdownMenuRadioGroup
                value={pageNumbersEnabled ? "enabled" : "disabled"}
                onValueChange={(value) =>
                  updatePdfOptions({
                    showHeaderFooter: value === "enabled",
                  })
                }
              >
                <DropdownMenuRadioItem
                  value="enabled"
                  className="data-[state=checked]:text-emerald-600 dark:data-[state=checked]:text-emerald-400"
                >
                  Enable
                </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
                <DropdownMenuRadioItem
                  value="disabled"
                  className="data-[state=checked]:text-rose-600 dark:data-[state=checked]:text-rose-400"
                >
                  Disable
                </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
              </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
              <DropdownMenuSeparator />
              <DropdownMenuLabel className="text-xs text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400">
                Alignment
              </DropdownMenuLabel>
              <DropdownMenuRadioGroup
                value={pageNumberAlign}
                onValueChange={(value) =>
                  updatePdfOptions({
                    pageNumberAlign: value as "left" | "center" | "right",
                  })
                }
              >
                <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="left" disabled={!pageNumbersEnabled}>
                  Left
                </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
                <DropdownMenuRadioItem
                  value="center"
                  disabled={!pageNumbersEnabled}
                >
                  Center
                </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
                <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="right" disabled={!pageNumbersEnabled}>
                  Right
                </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
              </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
            </DropdownMenuContent>
          </DropdownMenu>
        </>
      );
    }

                ) : (
                  <CheckCircle2 className="h-3.5 w-3.5 text-emerald-600 dark:text-emerald-400" />

                <span className="text-[11px] text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-300 whitespace-nowrap">
                  {autoSaveStatus === "saving"
                    ? "Saving..."

                </span>
              </div>
            )}
          </div>

          <div className="flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap justify-end w-full sm:w-auto">

    "use client";

    import { useEffect, useEffectEvent, useRef, useState } from "react";
    import { toast } from "sonner";
    import type { DesktopDocument, DiskDocument } from "@/lib/desktop";
    import { useEditorStore } from "@/stores/editor-store";

    type Recovery = { id: string; disk: DiskDocument };

    export function useWorkspaceFiles(active: boolean, documentId?: string) {
      const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
      const [recovery, setRecovery] = useState<Recovery>();
      const inFlight = useRef(false);
      const checking = useRef(0);

      async function run(operation: () => Promise<void>, error: string) {
        if (inFlight.current) return;
        inFlight.current = true;
        checking.current++;
        setBusy(true);
        try {
          await operation();
        } catch (cause) {
          toast.error(error, {
            description: cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : undefined,
          });
        } finally {
          inFlight.current = false;
          setBusy(false);
        }
      }

      function activeFile() {
        const state = useEditorStore.getState();
        return state.workspaceId && state.desktopDocumentId
          ? state.workspaceFiles[state.desktopDocumentId]
          : undefined;
      }

      const check = useEffectEvent(async () => {
        if (!active || inFlight.current || recovery || !documentId) return;
        const file = activeFile();
        const api = window.drymdfDesktop;
        if (!file || !api) return;
        const request = ++checking.current;
        try {
          const disk = await api.checkWorkspaceFile(file.id);
          if (request !== checking.current || activeFile()?.id !== file.id) return;
          if (
            disk.status === "missing" ||
            disk.document.revision !== file.revision
          ) {
            setRecovery({ id: file.id, disk });
          }
        } catch {
          if (request === checking.current) {
            toast.error("Couldn’t check the file on disk.", {
              id: "workspace-file-check",
            });
          }
        }
      });

      useEffect(() => {
        const onFocus = () => void check();
        onFocus();
        window.addEventListener("focus", onFocus);
        return () => {
          checking.current++;
          window.removeEventListener("focus", onFocus);
        };
      }, [active, documentId]);

      function save() {
        const file = activeFile();
        if (!file || recovery) return;
        void run(async () => {
          const api = window.drymdfDesktop!;
          const result =
            file.revision && file.content !== file.savedContent
              ? await api.saveWorkspaceFile(file.id, file.revision, file.content)
              : await api.checkWorkspaceFile(file.id);
          if (result.status === "saved") {
            // Keep edits made while the write was in flight in the recoverable draft.
            useEditorStore.getState().updateWorkspaceFile(file.id, {
              revision: result.revision,
              savedContent: file.content,
            });
            toast.success("Saved to disk", { id: "workspace-save" });
          } else if (
            result.status === "missing" ||
            result.document.revision !== file.revision
          ) {
            setRecovery({ id: file.id, disk: result });
          }
        }, "Couldn’t save the file.");
      }

      function chooseFiles(
        onChoose: (files: DesktopDocument[]) => void,
        multiple: boolean,
      ) {
        void run(async () => {
          const api = window.drymdfDesktop!;
          if (multiple) {
            const files = await api.chooseWorkspaceFiles();
            if (files.length) onChoose(files);
          } else {
            const file = await api.chooseMarkdown();
            if (file) onChoose([file]);
          }
        }, "Couldn’t add the selected files.");
      }

      function keep() {
        if (!recovery) return;
        if (recovery.disk.status === "available") {
          const { revision, content } = recovery.disk.document;
          useEditorStore.getState().updateWorkspaceFile(recovery.id, {
            revision,
            savedContent: content,
          });
        }
        setRecovery(undefined);
      }

      function reload() {
        if (recovery?.disk.status !== "available") return;
        const { id, disk } = recovery;
        void run(async () => {
          const latest = await window.drymdfDesktop!.checkWorkspaceFile(id);
          if (
            latest.status === "missing" ||
            latest.document.revision !== disk.document.revision
          ) {
            setRecovery({ id, disk: latest });
            return;
          }

    function isDarkHexColor(color: string): boolean {
      const normalized = color.replace("#", "");
      if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.test(normalized)) {
        return false;
      }

      const red = parseInt(normalized.slice(0, 2), 16);
      const green = parseInt(normalized.slice(2, 4), 16);
      const blue = parseInt(normalized.slice(4, 6), 16);
      const luminance = (0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue) / 255;
      return luminance < 0.5;
    }

    # DryMDF macOS Desktop Migration

    **Status, 26 November 2026.** The single-file editor, offline exports, desktop shell, and welcome wizard have passed local checks on Apple Silicon. The current DMG passed integrity verification and launched from a copy of the mounted image. The source baseline still needs a Git revision, and multi-file workspaces, page setup and export sheets, AI, and clean-Mac release checks are pending.

    ## Goal and release scope

    Ship DryMDF as an offline, single-user macOS app. Users should be able to install it from a DMG, open or write Markdown, preview it, and export PDF, HTML, and Markdown with no hosted backend.

    The first release targets **Apple Silicon** and uses a **free, unnotarized DMG** hosted on GitHub Releases. The download instructions will cover the first-launch **Open Anyway** prompt. Windows, Intel Macs, notarization, App Store distribution, automatic updates, and cloud sync are deferred. Record the oldest macOS version that passes installer and export testing before publishing.

    ## Architecture and code changes

    - **Desktop shell.** Add an Electron and Electron Forge workspace at `apps/desktop`. Package a static build of the editor from `apps/frontend` and launch into the editor. Reuse CodeMirror, the split-pane preview, theming, and Zustand. Check that routing, CSS, fonts, and other assets load from the installed bundle. Keep the current web build usable during migration.
    - **Local conversion.** Add a typed desktop bridge for conversion and file dialogs. Wire both the export handler in [the editor](../apps/frontend/src/app/editor/page.tsx) and the generated PDF path in [the preview pane](../apps/frontend/src/components/preview/pdf-preview-pane.tsx) to it. Desktop runtime dependencies should consist of the packaged app and its local assets. Drop the HTTP calls, Bull/Redis jobs, and WebSocket status polling from the desktop paths.
    - **PDF layout.** Reuse the existing [print styles and footer](../apps/backend/src/modules/pdf/print-layout.ts). Generate preview and export with the same hidden Chromium window and `webContents.printToPDF` pipeline. Bundle Mermaid, KaTeX CSS and fonts, syntax highlighting, and print fonts locally. Wait for diagrams, fonts, and supported images before printing. Discard stale preview results when the document or options change, and release temporary resources after each job.
    - **File access and safety.** Add native Open and Save dialogs and preserve draft recovery across restarts. Keep file reads and writes in the main process and validate requests from the renderer. Treat imported Markdown and Mermaid as untrusted content. Use sandboxed renderers, context isolation, a narrow preload bridge, sanitized HTML, and restricted navigation. Support relative images from the opened document's folder. Define a clear placeholder for unavailable remote images and verify that preview and export work offline.

    ## Work tracker

    | MAC-03 | Add native file dialogs, draft recovery, and safe handling of imported content and local images                      | MAC-01                        | 1–2 days | Done    | Native save, Unicode paths, image resolution, and draft recovery verified     |
