    # DryMDF desktop baseline

    [[projects/drymdf/DryMDF|DryMDF]] · [[projects/drymdf/facts/activity|DryMDF activity]] · [[projects/drymdf/facts/roadmap|DryMDF roadmap]] · [[projects/drymdf/decisions/2026-11-25-desktop-release-scope|Desktop release scope]]

    ## Working tree on 2026-11-25

    The local branch is `main` at `e7fb8c5`, matching the checkout’s `origin/main`. Desktop work is present in uncommitted changes and new files.

    - Electron and Electron Forge workspace, Apple Silicon packaging, preload bridge, and native file operations in `apps/desktop`.
    - Static editor build, desktop shell and setup, Two Sheets icon, native open and save, draft recovery and relative images, local Markdown/PDF previews, and PDF, HTML, and Markdown exports.
    - Desktop and web share print styles and footer generation from `apps/backend/src/modules/pdf/print-layout.ts`. The desktop PDF preview and export use the same local Chromium print path.

    ## Recorded verification

    - An installed Apple Silicon build on macOS 27.0.1 produced matching six-page A4 preview and PDF export with the network disabled. Mermaid, KaTeX fonts, code, and page numbering were checked.
    - The 0.1.0 release candidate DMG mounted and launched. Unicode paths, spaces, a relative PNG, draft recovery, native Save, cancel, failure, and retry were checked. A separate four-page fixture matched preview and export, and a Legal PDF verified background color and number placement. HTML opened offline and Markdown round-tripped exactly.
    - Frontend and backend builds passed in the recorded release candidate run. Web print styles and footer output were checked against the earlier implementation for default and customized options.
    - First-launch setup passed hidden-window tests for skip, reopen, saved preferences, and simulated notification opt-in and opt-out. Native permission prompts and banner delivery still need a visible clean-Mac test.
    - An earlier signing build failed to launch because Hardened Runtime caused macOS to reject the bundled Electron framework. The recorded rebuild adopted per-file ad-hoc signing and checks the executable before creating the image.

    ## Previous installer

    On 2026-11-25, the file at `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg` was 134,749,237 bytes. Its SHA-256 matched the sidecar:

    ```text
    8c9010e33e99aa3aa4355b469803fecd3644e9c2e4d7f7f322686e92354080e5
    ```

    The migration plan’s alias warning describes an earlier file at this path. Earlier mount and launch evidence refers to different checksums. The current bytes passed `hdiutil verify` on Apple Silicon macOS 27.0.1 on 2026-11-25. An installation and offline export run tied to a source revision and the tested image checksum is still pending.

    ## 26 November 2026 installer and MAC-09

    The ARM64 DMG at `apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg` is 134,752,026 bytes. Its SHA-256 matches the sidecar:

    ```text
    deaf8ed4afbf0e184bfa9be949a84444f6305a50d52e4107eb87f2acb8f8cbf9
    ```

    Built with Node 22.23.5 and pnpm 8.15.4 from the working tree on `main` at `e7fb8c5`. The desktop changes still need a committed source baseline.

    - Compared the light, dark, and compact editor against the Penpot boards. Reviewed the Two Sheets icon at 16, 32, and 128 pt.
    - In a temporary Electron profile, verified the file picker with simulated cancel, missing file, and Unicode path results. Tested Recents, sample rollback and editing, Skip Setup, keyboard focus, reduced motion and transparency, and draft recovery in a fresh process.
    - Generated and saved an actual PDF using simulated Save choices. Verified the first-PDF notification offer, both preferences, and subsequent notification requests with a simulated delivery service.
    - Production web and desktop builds, the backend build, and targeted frontend lint passed. On Apple Silicon macOS 27.0.1, the DMG passed integrity checks. A signed app copied from the mounted image opened Welcome, edited and previewed the sample, printed a local PDF, and restored the draft after relaunch.
    - Clean-Mac Gatekeeper, native notification permission and banner delivery, and the minimum supported macOS version are release checks.

**MAC-06 is complete and locally verified.** DryMDF now supports multi-file workspaces with independent drafts and relative images, even for files with the same name. Save updates only the active file. If an original moves or changes on disk, DryMDF offers **Locate File**, **Keep Draft**, or **Reload from Disk** as appropriate.

Settings now has a dedicated page. **Open**, **Save**, and **Export** share one aligned toolbar, and the Markdown/PDF controls stay in place when you switch modes. Switching files clears the previous PDF so you can’t mistake it for the current document.

    # Coding rules

    ## A PR does only its ticket's job (read before working in any repo)
    - Before writing code, state the ticket's problem in one line and the exact failing case(s). The PR fixes those cases and nothing else.
    - Make the smallest diff that fixes them. No widening to sibling phrasings or features, no refactors, no "while I'm here" changes.
    - Everything outside the ticket keeps the base branch's behaviour exactly. Run probes and sibling checks to prove nothing outside the scope changed, not to find more to fix.
    - Inside the ticket, the fix must work the way users actually phrase the failing case: natural variants, the question's own words echoed back, short forms. Test those too. That is the ticket's case, not widening.
    - When a review finds a gap outside the ticket's case, narrow: fall back to the base branch's behaviour. Don't extend the fix. Wider coverage goes in a follow-up issue, linked in the PR body.
    - Never narrow the ticket's own case to its literal phrasing, or retitle the PR to dodge a general rule. The ticket's case must work in its common form.
    - Test on the merge result with the current base branch, not only on the branch. Never push after approval without a new approval. No PR may depend on another unmerged PR.
    - The PR title and body describe the ticket's fix only. Don't grow them past it.
    - Review replies answer each finding and say what changed and how it is tested. They add no new scope and no extra work.
    - When briefing a subagent on a PR, put the ticket's exact case and this scope rule in the brief. List what must work as well as what must not change.

    ## Verify before every push (any repo)
    - **Mutation testing covers every alternative.** In a new or rewritten regex, word set or enum, drop each word, each character class and each branch on its own. Don't stop at the ones a reviewer named.
    - **"Changed" includes changed jobs.** If the push removes or skips a check, mutate and test the older line that is now the only guard for that case, even though its text didn't change.
    - **Time limits cut test scope, not mutants.** Keep sweeps short by running only the PR's own test files, never by skipping mutants.
    - **Fix the category, not the row.** When a probe or mutant finds a bad case, name the class it belongs to and fix that, with two or more tests from the class. Narrowing one word to dodge the found row is a one-case fix.

    ## Reuse before adding
    - Don't repeat code. Before writing a helper, branch or constant, search for an existing one and call it.
    - Change existing code at its call site rather than copying it into a new function.
    - Add a new block only when nothing existing can do the job. Keep it small, and have the old code use it too so there is one copy, not two.

    ## Use existing checkouts
    - Before cloning or downloading repository source, check for an existing local checkout, including in `~/Desktop/projects/open-source-contributes`. Use the checkout the user provides. Ask before downloading another copy.

    # Shared memory (all AI tools)
    There are two vaults. They are never mixed, and each is the single memory store for its own work. Do not keep a separate copy anywhere else.
    - **Personal vault: ~/Brain.** Personal and side projects only. Never write anything about JUTEQ work in it: no JUTEQ code, tickets, PRs, reviews, reviewers, decisions, customers, repos or notes, even when asked to "save this decision" while working in a JUTEQ directory. Do not add JUTEQ directories to its routing.md.
    - **JUTEQ vault: /Users/ajaymandal/Desktop/juteq/WorkVault.** Everything about JUTEQ work, all projects (argus, autorail, autorail-agents-v2, autorail-fe, autorail-mua and any new one). Same layout and rules as the personal vault, with its own _index/routing.md and _index/PROTOCOL.md.
    - Pick the vault from the working directory: anything under ~/Desktop/juteq is the JUTEQ vault, everything else is the personal vault. If it is unclear, ask. Never copy facts from one vault into the other.
    Rules for the routed vault (read its _index/PROTOCOL.md for the full text):
    - Isolation: the vault's _index/routing.md maps the working directory to exactly one project. Read only that project's hub and notes. Never read other projects' notes, Home.md, or search the whole vault, unless the user asks. If the directory is not in routing.md, ask which project to use.
    - Save durable facts to projects/<project>/facts/<slug>.md (only in the routed project) and decisions to projects/<project>/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md. One fact or decision per file.
    - Frontmatter on every note: name, description, project, type (user|feedback|project|reference|decision), source (claude|codex|gemini|other), date.
    - Link every note to its project hub and to related notes with wikilinks (double square brackets). A hub must link every note in its project. Update an existing note rather than adding a duplicate.
    - Skills live in ~/.agents/skills. MCP servers are defined in ~/Brain/_config/mcp/servers.json and hook scripts live in ~/Brain/_config/hooks; the JUTEQ vault has no tool config of its own.
    - Never store secrets or tokens in a vault.

         for(const p of mutants){assert(samples.some(v=>JSON.stringify(run(original,v))!==JSON.stringify(run(p,v))),source+' survived '+p); count++}

         const tryCases=(subs,samples)=>cases(name,p,subs.map(([a,b])=>p.replace(a,()=>b)),samples,f);
         if(p.includes('md|markdown'))tryCases([['md|',''],['|markdown','']],['a.MD','b.markdown','a.txt']);
         else if(p.includes('0-9a-fA-F'))tryCases([['0-9',''],['a-f',''],['A-F',''],['[0-9a-fA-F]','(?:)']],['123456','abcdef','ABCDEF','']);
         else if(p==='[?#]')tryCases([['?',''],['#',''],['[?#]','(?:)']],['a?b','a#b']);
         else if(p.includes('a-z0-9+.-'))tryCases([['[a-z]',''],['[a-z0-9+.-]','(?:)'],['a-z0-9','0-9'],['0-9',''],['+',''],['.',''],['-] ','] '].map(x=>x.trim())],['abc:','1:','a3:','a+:','a.:','a-:']);

    {
      "name": "@drymdf/desktop",
      "productName": "DryMDF",
      "version": "0.1.0",
      "description": "Offline Markdown editor and PDF exporter for macOS",
      "author": "Ajay Mandal",
      "license": "MIT",
      "private": true,
      "main": "main.cjs",
      "engines": {
        "node": "^22.12.0"
      },
      "scripts": {
        "build": "pnpm --filter @drymdf/frontend exec tsc ../backend/src/modules/pdf/print-layout.ts --outDir ../desktop/build --skipLibCheck --target es2022 --module commonjs && DRYMDF_DESKTOP=1 pnpm --filter @drymdf/frontend build",
        "start": "pnpm build && electron-forge start",
        "make": "pnpm build && electron-forge package --platform=darwin --arch=arm64 && sh make-dmg.sh"
      },
      "devDependencies": {
        "@electron-forge/cli": "7.11.2",
        "electron": "45.4.1"
      }
    }
    #!/bin/sh
    set -eu

    staging="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$staging"' EXIT

    ditto out/DryMDF-darwin-arm64/DryMDF.app "$staging/DryMDF.app"
    codesign --verify --deep --strict "$staging/DryMDF.app"
    ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$staging/DryMDF.app/Contents/MacOS/DryMDF" \
      -e 'if (!process.versions.electron || process.arch !== "arm64") process.exit(1)'
    ln -s /Applications "$staging/Applications"
    mkdir -p out/make
    build_output="$(mktemp -d out/make/.drymdf-build.XXXXXX)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$staging" "$build_output"' EXIT
    hdiutil create -volname DryMDF -srcfolder "$staging" -format UDZO \
      "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg"
    (cd "$build_output" && shasum -a 256 DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg > DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256)
    mv -f "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg" out/make/
    mv -f "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256" out/make/

## Assistant

On PR #4, **both Vercel checks passed**. The red check is GitHub Actions `CI / quality`. GitHub says the job never started because the account is locked due to a billing issue. Lint never ran. Disconnecting Vercel will stop future previews, but the GitHub Actions billing issue needs a separate fix. [Failed quality job](https://github.com/ajay-mandal/DryMDF/actions/runs/45772855200/job/139749383153)

**To retire Vercel for DryMDF**, there are two independent deployment paths to turn off:

1. In the `drymdf-frontend` Vercel project, open **Settings → Git → Connected Git Repository → Disconnect**. This stops the integration from creating previews on future pushes. [Project Git settings](https://vercel.com/0xajaymandals-projects/drymdf-frontend/settings/git) · [Vercel instructions](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-settings)
2. Remove `deploy-frontend-dev.yml` and `deploy-frontend.yml` from `.github/workflows` on the branches where they run. They explicitly invoke the Vercel CLI on pushes to `development` and `main`, independently of the integration. If either branch requires a Vercel status check, remove that requirement from its GitHub ruleset too.

**For open-source desktop CI, I’d choose Woodpecker CI if you have a dedicated Apple Silicon Mac.** Its macOS agent can run the existing Electron Forge packaging command directly. The local backend executes jobs as the agent’s OS user, so use an isolated build machine for trusted builds. If you don’t want to maintain a Mac, the simpler option is to resolve the GitHub billing issue and use its hosted `macos-15` ARM64 runner. [Woodpecker macOS backend](https://woodpecker-ci.org/docs/administration/configuration/backends/local) · [GitHub runner specifications](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-where-workflows-run/choose-the-runner-for-a-job)

For DryMDF, I’d use this pipeline with either provider:

| Trigger           | What runs                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pull request      | Install from the frozen lockfile, run frontend lint and type checks, and build the desktop renderer on Node 22. The Electron app still ships that frontend code. |
| Release candidate | On Apple Silicon, run `pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make`, verify the DMG and checksum, and retain both as artifacts.                                           |
| Release approval  | Smoke-test that DMG on a clean Mac, then publish the **same tested DMG and checksum** to GitHub Releases.                                                        |

I checked the live PR and repository configuration. No deployment settings or workflows were changed.

        # DryMDF desktop CI

        Woodpecker runs on your hardware. This configuration uses a local SQLite volume and an Apple Silicon build agent. It needs no hosted CI minutes or paid storage service. The Mac and its internet connection must be available during builds.

        ## Connect GitHub

        1. Route a stable HTTPS address through your existing reverse proxy or tunnel to port 8120 on the server host. GitHub delivers webhooks to that address. Keep the agent connection on loopback.
        2. Register a [GitHub OAuth app](https://github.com/settings/applications/new) under the personal account. Use the public address for its homepage and append `/authorize` for its callback.
        3. In a private environment file outside the checkout, set `WOODPECKER_HOST`, `WOODPECKER_GITHUB_CLIENT`, and `WOODPECKER_GITHUB_SECRET`. Restrict the file to its owner. Start the dashboard from the repo root:

           ```sh
           docker compose --env-file ~/.config/drymdf-ci/server.env -f ci/woodpecker/compose.yaml up -d
           ```

        4. Sign in as `ajay-mandal` and activate `ajay-mandal/DryMDF`. Enable push, pull request and tag hooks. Require approval for forked PRs. Review the entire proposed change before approving a run because the native agent executes contributor code directly. Leave repository trust disabled. Use a dedicated build account or isolated macOS VM with no personal credentials.
        5. Under **User settings → Agents**, register a personal agent. Restrict it to this repository using the repo filter. On the build account, install the matching [Woodpecker agent for Darwin ARM64](https://github.com/woodpecker-ci/woodpecker/releases/tag/v3.21.0), Git, Node 22.12 or later within 22.x, pnpm 8.15.4, and the GitHub CLI. Provide the agent token privately as `WOODPECKER_AGENT_SECRET`. Start the agent on the same Mac as the server:

           ```sh
           WOODPECKER_SERVER=127.0.0.1:9120 WOODPECKER_BACKEND=local woodpecker-agent agent
           ```

           Keep the agent running under the build account. Check **Agents** for its online status.
        6. Add a repository secret named `drymdf_release_token` in Woodpecker. Use a fine-grained GitHub token limited to this repository with Contents read/write and restrict the Woodpecker secret to **tag** events. Limit creation of release tags to maintainers.

        ## Track a build or release

        Open DryMDF in the dashboard to see the commit and each step's logs. PRs targeting development or main and pushes to those branches check code quality, build the Apple Silicon installer and verify its checksum and disk image. After activation, redeliver a GitHub webhook or push a commit to see the first run.

        A maintainer pushing a new version tag such as `v0.1.0` runs the same checks, then uploads the verified DMG and SHA-256 file to a draft GitHub Release. Download that draft, perform the clean-Mac acceptance checks in the [migration plan](../../docs/DESKTOP_MIGRATION_PLAN.md), then publish that draft in GitHub. An existing release with the same tag makes the upload step fail. Inspect its assets before retrying.

    # DryMDF desktop CI

    Woodpecker runs on your hardware. This configuration uses a local SQLite volume and an Apple Silicon build agent. It needs no hosted CI minutes or paid storage service. The Mac and its internet connection must be available during builds.

    ## Connect GitHub

    1. Route a stable HTTPS address through your existing reverse proxy or tunnel to port 8120 on the server host. GitHub delivers webhooks to that address. Keep the agent connection on loopback.
    2. Register a [GitHub OAuth app](https://github.com/settings/applications/new) under the personal account. Use the public address for its homepage and append `/authorize` for its callback.
    3. In a private environment file outside the checkout, set `WOODPECKER_HOST`, `WOODPECKER_GITHUB_CLIENT`, and `WOODPECKER_GITHUB_SECRET`. Restrict the file to its owner. Start the dashboard from the repo root:

       ```sh
       docker compose --env-file ~/.config/drymdf-ci/server.env -f ci/woodpecker/compose.yaml up -d
       ```

    4. Sign in as `ajay-mandal` and activate `ajay-mandal/DryMDF`. Enable push, pull request and tag hooks. Require approval for forked PRs. Review the entire proposed change before approving a run because the native agent executes contributor code directly. Leave repository trust disabled. Use a dedicated build account or isolated macOS VM with no personal credentials.
    5. Under **User settings → Agents**, register a personal agent. Restrict it to this repository using the repo filter. On the build account, install the matching [Woodpecker agent for Darwin ARM64](https://github.com/woodpecker-ci/woodpecker/releases/tag/v3.21.0), Git, Node 22.12 or later within 22.x, pnpm 8.15.4, and the GitHub CLI. Provide the agent token privately as `WOODPECKER_AGENT_SECRET`. Start the agent on the same Mac as the server:

       ```sh
       mkdir -p ~/.config/drymdf-ci
       WOODPECKER_AGENT_CONFIG_FILE="$HOME/.config/drymdf-ci/agent.conf" \
         WOODPECKER_SERVER=127.0.0.1:9120 WOODPECKER_BACKEND=local woodpecker-agent
       ```

       Keep the agent running under the build account. Check **Agents** for its online status.

    6. Add a repository secret named `drymdf_release_token` in Woodpecker. Use a fine-grained GitHub token limited to this repository with Contents read/write and restrict the Woodpecker secret to **tag** events. Limit creation of release tags to maintainers.

    ## Track a build or release

    Open DryMDF in the dashboard to see the commit and each step's logs. PRs targeting development or main and pushes to those branches check code quality, build the Apple Silicon installer and verify its checksum and disk image. After activation, redeliver a GitHub webhook or push a commit to see the first run.

    A maintainer pushing a new version tag such as `v0.1.0` runs the same checks, then uploads the verified DMG and SHA-256 file to a draft GitHub Release. Download that draft, perform the clean-Mac acceptance checks in the [migration plan](../../docs/DESKTOP_MIGRATION_PLAN.md), then publish that draft in GitHub. An existing release with the same tag makes the upload step fail. Inspect its assets before retrying.

    when:
      - event: [push, pull_request]
        branch: [development, main]

    labels:
      platform: darwin/arm64
      backend: local

    steps:
      - name: install
        image: bash
        environment:
          PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD: "true"
          HUSKY: "0"
        commands:
          - node -e 'if (process.versions.node.split(".")[0] !== "22" || Number(process.versions.node.split(".")[1]) < 12) process.exit(1)'
          - test "$(pnpm --version)" = 8.15.4
          - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: quality
        image: bash
        commands:
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/frontend lint
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/backend lint:check
          - pnpm type-check
          - pnpm format:check
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/backend build

      - name: package
        image: bash
        commands:
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make

      - name: verify-installer
        image: bash
        commands:
          - cd apps/desktop/out/make
          - shasum -a 256 -c DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256
          - hdiutil verify DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg

      - name: draft-release
        image: bash
        when:
          - event: tag

        environment:

        commands:

    # personal-vault-sync: the personal vault

    `~/Brain` is the single memory store for all personal and side-project work, for every AI tool. It follows the LLM-wiki pattern: **raw sources** (immutable) feed **notes** (the wiki, written by AI), governed by **rules** (`~/Brain/_index/PROTOCOL.md`, then this skill). If this file and the protocol disagree, the protocol wins.

    Set `source` in every note to your own name: `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` or `other`. It is how the user tells who wrote a note.

    ## 0. Guard: not JUTEQ
    Run `pwd`. If it is under `~/Desktop/juteq`, stop and say: "This is JUTEQ work. Use the work-vault-sync skill and ~/Desktop/juteq/WorkVault." Write nothing. Never write JUTEQ work into ~/Brain.

    ## 1. Route to one project
    1. Read `~/Brain/_index/routing.md`. Match the working directory (longest prefix wins). If nothing matches, use the "What it holds" column to propose a project and ask the user. Never guess.
    2. Read that project's hub `~/Brain/projects/<project>/<project>.md` (Status / Next first), then only the notes it links that the task needs.
    3. Do not search the whole vault, do not open `Home.md`, do not follow a link into another project (a link to another project's hub is the only allowed hop, when the task is about that relationship).

    ## 2. Where each thing goes
    | What | Where | Template |
    |---|---|---|
    | Progress on a feature: done, pending, waits on | `facts/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>-progress.md`, one per feature, updated in place | `assets/progress.md` |
    | A decision the user made | `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` | `assets/decision.md` |
    | A bug fixed | `facts/YYYY-MM-DD-bug-<slug>.md` | `assets/bug.md` |
    | A fact or reference (where something lives, how it is set up) | `facts/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` | `assets/fact.md` |
    | A rule or preference about how to work | `facts/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, `type: feedback` | `assets/fact.md` |
    | A source document: transcript, export, PDF, web clip, chat log | `raw/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-raw.<ext>`, never edited; digest it into a note | none (copy as is) |
    | An image embedded in a note | `attachments/<slug>-YYYY-MM-DD.<ext>` | none |
    | A change to the project (what you just did to the vault) | one line appended to the project's log note | `assets/log.md` |
    | Knowledge that spans projects (only when the user asks) | `~/Brain/concepts/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, listed in `concepts/concepts.md` | `assets/concept.md` |
    | Unsorted capture with no known project | `~/Brain/inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` (`project: inbox`) | `assets/fact.md` |

    Never create other folders. Never write to another project's folder.

    ## 3. Ingest (saving)
    1. Work out what to record from the conversation. If a value is unclear, ask one short question or write "not stated, to confirm". Never invent a value, date, decider or PR number.
    2. **Source first.** If there is a source document (the user pasted or points to a file), copy it to `raw/` unchanged, named `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-raw.<ext>`, then `chmod a-w` it. Never overwrite or edit a raw file; a changed source is a new dated file. Add it to the hub under "Raw sources": `- [[name-raw]]: what it is, digested in [[note]]` (non-`.md` files are linked with the extension). Never save secrets or personal data; look first.
    3. **Then the note.** One fact or decision per file. Check the hub and file names, and update an existing note instead of duplicating. Start from the template. File name `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`: date first (from `date +%F`; the creation day, or for a decision the day decided), lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, unique across the vault, never a date at the end. A tracker keeps its file name when updated; only its `date` field and Log move.
    4. **Then the hub.** In the same change add the note under "Facts" or "Decisions" as `- [[name]]: one-line hook`, newest first. Update "Status / Next" (done, pending and what each waits on, next step) and the hub's `date`.
    5. **Then the log.** Append one line at the bottom of the project's log note: `## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <what changed> | <links>` with op = ingest, decision, fix, query, lint or restructure. Never edit old entries. (drymdf and penpot keep their existing dated logs, linked from the hub's "Log" section.)
    6. Decisions need a named decider; a remark with no known source is not a decision, log it in the progress note as "suggested, by whom not stated, to confirm".
    7. Progress notes keep Done (`- [x]`) and Pending (`- [ ]`); each pending item says who or what it waits on ("not stated" when unknown). Moving an item adds "(done YYYY-MM-DD)"; add a dated Log line; never delete history.
    8. Never store secrets, tokens, keys, passwords or connection strings. Name where a secret lives, never its value.

    ### Frontmatter (exactly these fields, this order, first in the file)
    ```
    ---
    name: 2026-11-25-example-slug
    description: "One line, always in double quotes: what the note is and when it is relevant"
    project: <project folder name>
    type: <user|feedback|project|reference|decision>
    source: <claude|codex|gemini|other>
    date: 2026-11-25
    ---
    ```
    `name` = the file name without `.md`. Escape an inner `"` as `\"`: an unquoted `description` containing `: ` breaks the block and Obsidian shows red raw text. `date` is the unquoted day of the last update. Do not delete extra fields an existing note has; add none to new notes. Hubs use `type: project`.

    ### Links
    Wikilinks by name only: `[[2026-11-25-example-slug]]`. No `.md`, no path, no `[text](file.md)`, no link to a missing note. Every note links its hub `[[<project>]]` and related notes. Notes link only inside their own project; the one exception is a link to another project's hub for a source-code or design-reference relationship the user asked for. Renaming a note changes its `name` and every link to it, in the same change.

    ## 4. Query (answering from the vault)
    1. Route (section 1), read the hub, then the notes it points to. Answer from them and cite note names.
    2. If the answer is new, durable knowledge (a comparison, a conclusion), file it back as a note (section 3) and add a `query` line to the log. Do not file trivial answers.
    3. If notes disagree or look stale, say so and ask which is right; do not silently pick one.

    ## 5. Lint
    `bash ~/.agents/skills/personal-vault-sync/scripts/check-vault.sh --lint <project>` prints WARN lines (never fails): notes not updated for 30+ days, open "to confirm" or "not stated" markers, dead local paths, raw sources no note digests, writable raw files, inbox items waiting. Report them to the user; fix only what the user approves, and log a `lint` line.

    ## 6. Check, then report
    1. Run `bash ~/.agents/skills/personal-vault-sync/scripts/check-vault.sh <project>` (also `concepts` or `inbox` when you wrote there; vault defaults to `~/Brain`, override with `$BRAIN`). Fix every failure until it exits 0.
    2. Tell the user briefly: each file written or updated (full path), raw sources and images saved, anything marked "to confirm", anything not saved and why.
    3. Do not run git commands for the vault.

    ## 7. Sync a whole session (when the user says "vault sync", "sync vault" or "update the vault")
    The user wants you to go and write down where things stand. Apply sections 1 to 6 in one pass, then refresh the navigation root.
    1. **Collect from this session only** (not from other sessions): status (done, pending, what each waits on, next step); decisions (who, when, where, why); rules and preferences the user stated; activity (changes, checks, blockers, dated); raw sources the user gave or pointed to; facts and bugs fixed. If the session produced nothing durable, say so and write nothing. Never invent a value: write "not stated, to confirm".
    2. **Write in this order:** raw files first (read-only, no secrets or personal data), then notes (update existing ones), then the hub (list new notes and raw files, rewrite Status / Next, set `date`), then one log line per change.
    3. **Update the navigation root.** `_index/Home.md` is the main navigation root: one line per project, `- [[<project>]]: what it holds. Status (YYYY-MM-DD): one line from the hub's Status / Next`. Update the line of every project you wrote to, add a line for a new project, keep `[[concepts]]` listed, set `date`. Change `_index/routing.md` only when the session created a project or changed a directory mapping (row plus its "What it holds" cell). Hub links only in Home, never links to notes. Never edit `PROTOCOL.md`.
    4. **Check both** until they exit 0: `check-vault.sh <project>` and `check-vault.sh _index`. Report each file written (full path), raw files saved, Home or routing changes, "to confirm" items and anything not saved.

    ## Never
    - Never edit `_index/PROTOCOL.md`. Edit `routing.md` and `Home.md` only in a sync (section 7) or when the user asks.
    - Never edit or delete a raw file, and never delete a note without the user's approval.
    - Never write JUTEQ work here.

    # DryMDF

    DryMDF edits Markdown, previews documents, and exports printable files. The active milestone is the offline macOS release. The web app remains part of the project.

    **Design:** before changing any design, read [[2026-11-26-design-reference]] and [[penpot-personal]].

    ## Status / Next

    | --- | --- |
    | Web app | Editor, Markdown and PDF previews, export, and deployment configuration are committed on `main`. |

    | Single-file macOS app | MAC-01–04 are complete according to the local verification log. The desktop migration is in the working tree. |
    | Desktop UI and welcome | MAC-09 passed local wizard, layout, and mounted-DMG checks. The first successful PDF save can offer optional notifications. |

    | Desktop release | The current ARM64 DMG passed image and mounted-copy smoke checks. A committed baseline and clean-Mac release checks remain. |

    - [[2026-11-25-activity|DryMDF activity]] records development, design, testing, pull requests, and release activity.

## Assistant

Yes. With the current Woodpecker setup, **your Mac must be awake and online during builds**. If you host the dashboard on the same Mac, it also needs to be online to receive GitHub webhooks and show build history.

**After a build**, what happens depends on what triggered it:

- **Push or pull request:** Woodpecker builds and verifies the `.dmg`, then reports success or failure. The current workflow doesn’t upload a downloadable copy for these runs.
- **Version tag such as `v0.1.0`:** Once the GitHub connection is active, Woodpecker uploads the `.dmg` and its checksum to a **draft GitHub Release**. You test it and click **Publish release**. From then on, people download it from GitHub even when your Mac is off. [DryMDF Releases](https://github.com/ajay-mandal/DryMDF/releases)

**For a Vercel-like experience, I’d use GitHub-hosted Actions for DryMDF.** You push code, GitHub starts an Apple Silicon Mac, and you see progress on the PR. The workflow can attach a downloadable installer to each PR run and create a draft release on version tags. Your Mac can be off throughout. GitHub’s standard `macos-15` ARM64 runner is free for public repositories. [GitHub-hosted runner details](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners)

The blocker is your **GitHub account billing lock**. GitHub reported that it prevented PR #4’s job from starting, even before lint ran. If Billing & Licensing shows no outstanding issue, GitHub directs you to Support to clear the lock. Once cleared, hosted Actions is the simplest fit for the workflow you described. [GitHub account unlock guide](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/how-tos/troubleshooting/locked-account)

    when:
      - event: [push, pull_request]
        branch: [development, main]
      - event: tag
        ref: refs/tags/v*

    labels:
      platform: darwin/arm64
      backend: local

    steps:
      - name: install
        image: bash
        environment:
          PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD: "true"
          HUSKY: "0"
        commands:
          - node -e 'if (process.versions.node.split(".")[0] !== "22" || Number(process.versions.node.split(".")[1]) < 12) process.exit(1)'
          - test "$(pnpm --version)" = 8.15.4
          - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: quality
        image: bash
        commands:
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/frontend lint
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/backend lint:check
          - pnpm type-check
          - pnpm format:check
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/backend build

      - name: package
        image: bash
        commands:
          - pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make

      - name: verify-installer
        image: bash
        commands:
          - cd apps/desktop/out/make
          - shasum -a 256 -c DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256
          - hdiutil verify DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg

      - name: draft-release
        image: bash
        when:
          - event: tag
            ref: refs/tags/v*
        environment:
          GH_TOKEN:
            from_secret: drymdf_release_token
        commands:
          - cd apps/desktop/out/make
          - gh release create "$CI_COMMIT_TAG" DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256 --repo ajay-mandal/DryMDF --verify-tag --draft --title "DryMDF $CI_COMMIT_TAG" --generate-notes
    #!/bin/sh
    set -eu

    staging="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$staging"' EXIT

    ditto out/DryMDF-darwin-arm64/DryMDF.app "$staging/DryMDF.app"
    codesign --verify --deep --strict "$staging/DryMDF.app"
    ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$staging/DryMDF.app/Contents/MacOS/DryMDF" \
      -e 'if (!process.versions.electron || process.arch !== "arm64") process.exit(1)'
    ln -s /Applications "$staging/Applications"
    mkdir -p out/make
    build_output="$(mktemp -d out/make/.drymdf-build.XXXXXX)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$staging" "$build_output"' EXIT
    hdiutil create -volname DryMDF -srcfolder "$staging" -format UDZO \
      "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg"
    (cd "$build_output" && shasum -a 256 DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg > DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256)
    mv -f "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg" out/make/
    mv -f "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256" out/make/

## User

so now we can have release dmg in github hosted for others to download?

## Assistant

Yes. **GitHub Releases can host the DryMDF installer for others to download**, even when your Mac is offline.

The verified DMG is currently a **PR artifact** that expires after seven days. To make it a public release:

1. Merge PR #4 and push a version tag such as `v0.1.0` on the merged commit.
2. GitHub Actions builds and verifies the Apple Silicon DMG, then attaches it and its SHA-256 checksum to a **draft release**.
3. Test the draft installer on a clean Mac, then click **Publish release**.

After publication, anyone can download it from [DryMDF Releases](https://github.com/ajay-mandal/DryMDF/releases/latest). The current installer targets Apple Silicon and is ad-hoc signed, so macOS may ask users to choose **Open Anyway** on first launch.

## Assistant

There’s no single open-source standard for DMG names. A common convention is **`App-Version-Architecture.dmg`**. Joplin, for example, includes the version and `arm64` in its Apple Silicon installer name. [Joplin releases](https://github.com/laurent22/joplin/releases)

For DryMDF, I’d use:

- **Git tag:** `v0.1.0`
- **Release title:** `DryMDF 0.1.0`
- **Installer:** `DryMDF-0.1.0-arm64.dmg`
- **Checksum:** `DryMDF-0.1.0-arm64.dmg.sha256`

The version makes the file identifiable after download, and `arm64` identifies Apple Silicon. The GitHub prerelease flag is appropriate while the clean-Mac Gatekeeper check is pending. [GitHub release guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository)

I confirmed the interrupted rename left the published assets unchanged. I’d keep the current `DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg` link working and adopt versioned names for future releases.

    name: Desktop CI

    on:
      pull_request:
        branches: [development, main]
      push:
        branches: [development, main]
        tags: ["v*"]

    permissions:
      contents: read

    jobs:
      quality:
        runs-on: macos-15
        env:
          PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD: "true"
          HUSKY: "0"
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: "22"
              cache: pnpm
          - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          - name: Check code quality
            run: |
              pnpm --filter @drymdf/frontend lint
              pnpm --filter @drymdf/backend lint:check
              pnpm type-check
              pnpm format:check
              pnpm --filter @drymdf/backend build
          - name: Package Apple Silicon installer
            run: pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make
          - name: Verify installer
            working-directory: apps/desktop/out/make
            run: |
              shasum -a 256 -c DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256
              hdiutil verify DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: DryMDF-mac-arm64
              path: |
                apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg
                apps/desktop/out/make/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 7
              compression-level: 0

      draft-release:
        needs: quality
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: DryMDF-mac-arm64
          - name: Create draft release
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
            run: |
              sha256sum -c DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256
              gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256 \
                --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --draft --generate-notes --title "DryMDF $GITHUB_REF_NAME"
    #!/bin/sh
    set -eu

    staging="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$staging"' EXIT

    ditto out/DryMDF-darwin-arm64/DryMDF.app "$staging/DryMDF.app"
    codesign --verify --deep --strict "$staging/DryMDF.app"
    ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$staging/DryMDF.app/Contents/MacOS/DryMDF" \
      -e 'if (!process.versions.electron || process.arch !== "arm64") process.exit(1)'
    ln -s /Applications "$staging/Applications"
    mkdir -p out/make
    build_output="$(mktemp -d out/make/.drymdf-build.XXXXXX)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$staging" "$build_output"' EXIT
    hdiutil create -volname DryMDF -srcfolder "$staging" -format UDZO \
      "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg"
    (cd "$build_output" && shasum -a 256 DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg > DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256)
    mv -f "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg" out/make/
    mv -f "$build_output/DryMDF-mac-arm64.dmg.sha256" out/make/

    # Coding rules

    ## A PR does only its ticket's job (read before working in any repo)
    - Before writing code, state the ticket's problem in one line and the exact failing case(s). The PR fixes those cases and nothing else.
    - Make the smallest diff that fixes them. No widening to sibling phrasings or features, no refactors, no "while I'm here" changes.
    - Everything outside the ticket keeps the base branch's behaviour exactly. Run probes and sibling checks to prove nothing outside the scope changed, not to find more to fix.
    - Inside the ticket, the fix must work the way users actually phrase the failing case: natural variants, the question's own words echoed back, short forms. Test those too. That is the ticket's case, not widening.
    - When a review finds a gap outside the ticket's case, narrow: fall back to the base branch's behaviour. Don't extend the fix. Wider coverage goes in a follow-up issue, linked in the PR body.
    - Never narrow the ticket's own case to its literal phrasing, or retitle the PR to dodge a general rule. The ticket's case must work in its common form.
    - Test on the merge result with the current base branch, not only on the branch. Never push after approval without a new approval. No PR may depend on another unmerged PR.
    - The PR title and body describe the ticket's fix only. Don't grow them past it.
    - Review replies answer each finding and say what changed and how it is tested. They add no new scope and no extra work.
    - When briefing a subagent on a PR, put the ticket's exact case and this scope rule in the brief. List what must work as well as what must not change.

    ## Verify before every push (any repo)
    - **Mutation testing covers every alternative.** In a new or rewritten regex, word set or enum, drop each word, each character class and each branch on its own. Don't stop at the ones a reviewer named.
    - **"Changed" includes changed jobs.** If the push removes or skips a check, mutate and test the older line that is now the only guard for that case, even though its text didn't change.
    - **Time limits cut test scope, not mutants.** Keep sweeps short by running only the PR's own test files, never by skipping mutants.
    - **Fix the category, not the row.** When a probe or mutant finds a bad case, name the class it belongs to and fix that, with two or more tests from the class. Narrowing one word to dodge the found row is a one-case fix.

    ## Reuse before adding
    - Don't repeat code. Before writing a helper, branch or constant, search for an existing one and call it.
    - Change existing code at its call site rather than copying it into a new function.
    - Add a new block only when nothing existing can do the job. Keep it small, and have the old code use it too so there is one copy, not two.

    ## Use existing checkouts
    - Before cloning or downloading repository source, check for an existing local checkout, including in `~/Desktop/projects/open-source`. Use the checkout the user provides. Ask before downloading another copy.

Never write anything about JUTEQ work in it: no JUTEQ code, tickets, PRs, reviews, reviewers, decisions, customers, repos or notes, even when asked to "save this decision" while working in a JUTEQ directory. Do not add JUTEQ directories to its routing.md.

    ## Next — Phase 0

    1. Review the existing desktop and shared print changes and capture the intended source in a dedicated baseline branch and commit. Keep generated installers and local caches out of that baseline.
    2. Use Node 22.12+ within 22.x and the pinned pnpm version. Node 22.23.5 is available at `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin/node`. Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then use `pnpm --filter @drymdf/desktop make`.
    3. Install the resulting DMG from a mounted image. Reopen the draft, verify multi-page offline PDF preview/export parity, and check standalone HTML and Markdown round-trip. Run the normal frontend and backend builds. Log the source commit, DMG SHA-256, macOS version, and results.
    4. Continue with MAC-10 page setup and export sheets. MAC-07 provider setup can proceed independently after Phase 0.

    Deployment is complete for the public v0.1.0 prerelease. Feature development is on hold. Clean-Mac qualification is pending for stable release. See [[2026-11-27-v010-release-progress]].

    # DryMDF desktop release scope

    [[drymdf]] · [[2026-11-25-roadmap]] · [[2026-11-25-desktop-baseline]]

    The first desktop release targets a single-user, offline editor on Apple Silicon macOS. Publish a free, unnotarized DMG through GitHub Releases with its SHA-256, supported macOS version, and first-launch instructions. Determine the oldest supported macOS through installer and export testing. Editing and PDF, HTML, and Markdown export work with AI disabled.

    The redesigned MVP includes multi-file workspaces, the Penpot editor and export flows, and opt-in AI through Ollama, LM Studio, or one hosted OpenAI-compatible provider. Defer Windows, Intel Macs, notarization, App Store distribution, automatic updates, cloud sync, cross-file AI writes, workspace indexing, AI tool execution, and additional hosted adapters.

A separate four-page fixture matched preview and export, and a Legal PDF verified background color and number placement. HTML opened offline and Markdown round-tripped exactly.
